Every release starts with its Headline: the single best feature that release brought (Boss, 2026-10-10). The sections under it keep the full record. The headline features still to come are listed in the README.

[8.0.3731] - 2026-11-08

Headline: A test now fails when install.sh or update.sh could miss a library that setup.py requires.

Changed

  • test_install_python_deps.py checks the one list both scripts use. install.sh and update.sh --check both run scripts/install-python-deps.sh; the test fails if either stops doing so, if the list differs from setup.py's requirements, if psutil is missing, or if a listed library is not pinned in requirements.lock and requirements-server.lock.

[8.0.3730] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The update's library check now installs psutil, so the work queue's workers start again after the memory gate (PERF.254).

Changed

  • psutil is on update.sh's list of required libraries (scripts/install-python-deps.sh). PERF.254 added psutil to setup.py and the lock files but not to the script's list, so an existing install never got it and every worker died at its start on import psutil (exit status 1), which stopped the math check at stage 4 of the update. --check now sees it missing and installs it from the lock.

[8.0.3729] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The class and systems censuses are re-tagged after trains 15 to 18: 18 new flags are tagged with their reasons, 51 stale tags are removed, and the life census passes without a flag.

Changed

  • Census re-tag on epoch 140 (GEN.1353). The three live censuses ran on the tree after train 18 (GEN.1397 included). The class census raised 17 new flags: nine in moon cells (Class D too common in four cells, and the life ceiling of four moon cells), eight in planet shares (A0V ecosphere tiers Red and Yellow and microbial ceiling, F5V ecosphere no ceiling at 0.902 against a range top of 0.736, F5V hot microbial ceiling, A0V cold Class V and G2V ecosphere Class N absent). All are tagged GEN.1353 with the numbers; the F5V ecosphere share is the one large move, likely from GEN.1397, and the TEST.660 re-baseline decides whether it is a fault. The systems census raised one flag, M2V photosynthetic life at 0.360 against a floor of 0.397, tagged GEN.1353. The life census raised a hang of 6 systems over 60 s when it ran beside two other censuses; run alone it passes with no flag, so it was load and not a fault. 18 class, 30 systems and 3 occurrence tags whose range holds again are removed. Only test data changes; the ranges stay until the re-baseline after the last 8.1 train (TEST.660).

generation-output: unchanged

[8.0.3728] - 2026-11-08

Headline: A warm-up or another bulk command can no longer block the site: waiting jobs are now ordered by a fair-share scheduler, with places kept for the site.

Added

  • A fair-share scheduler on the memory gate (OPS.130, queue/scheduler.py). A job waiting for room is a ticket, ordered by its class (interactive 100, node prefetch 90, long 80, a run's units 40, the maintenance lane 30), plus a rise for each second it waited, less a penalty for the share of recent system time its kind has used. A job that has waited 600 s outranks a new job of any class, so nothing starves. A lower job goes ahead of a higher one that has no room (the host is not left idle), unless the higher one has waited 120 s, when the room is kept for it. The scheduler reads the same load and memory as the gate.
  • Cores are kept for the site's places (half a core a place, at most a quarter of the host) against the bulk and maintenance lanes, as memory already was.

Changed

  • Every worker and memorygate.hold use the scheduler. PLANETGEN_MEMORY_GATE=0 still turns the gate off.
  • Generated output is unchanged.

[8.0.3727] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The block light totals are now the last stage of a galaxy run, and their bar moves through all three parts.

Changed

  • Block lights last (PERF.251). galaxy_stages puts "Make the block light totals" after the settling and the run blocks instead of after the nebula field. The totals add up only stars and phenomena that are not built yet, so they were redone for nothing as the backfill, population and settling built them; made last they are made once from what is left. The stage list, run_galaxy's followers, commands' stage numbers and the design docs (redis-and-the-work-queue.md, command-inventory.md) follow the new order.
  • The uncharted placeholder rows come after the backfill (PERF.252). The totals stage writes the uncharted sector rows, which the bright-star backfill used to count as sectors the run had just made: on a small galaxy (3e7 solar masses, radius 6 pc) it planned 573,713 backfill targets and 34,707 sky cells from 19 real sectors and drew 16,471 bright stars where the run's own sectors give 1,037; on a big galaxy that is millions of rows, the 900 s job limit and an out-of-memory kill. With the totals last the backfill opens on the run's real sectors only, and store.sector_centers_since now counts charted sectors only (a cell with no chart ledger row is a placeholder), so a placeholder can never be taken for a run sector again. generation-output: changed
  • The bar moves all the way. "Making the block light totals" counts 100 steps in three parts (the units 70, the levels above the units 15, the uncharted rows the rest) and says the share done in its log line, so it no longer sits at one value through the longest part.
  • Tests. test_stages.py has the new stage numbers and a test that the block lights stage is last; test_block_lights.py checks that the bar moves in all three parts.

[8.0.3726] - 2026-11-08

Headline: A carbon-rich rocky world (a star with C/O of 0.8 or more) now carries moissanite (silicon carbide) and cohenite (iron carbide) deposits; oxygen-rich worlds never do.

Added

  • Two carbide deposit types (GEN.1423, physics/carbide_deposits.py). After the ore pass each rocky planet, moon and rogue planet is assessed for moissanite_crust (the SiC of the carbon rock, grade 0.71 to 0.95, the share the bulk draw's graphite range leaves) and cohenite_metal (Fe3C in the carbon-saturated metal, grade 0.30 to 0.64). Both are rows of the existing deposit tables (no column, no migration); a body with silicate rock has both rows absent_by_state. Stand-ins CH1 to CH3 in section 6.235.

Changed

  • The stored deposits of every rocky body gain two rows, so the next epoch is a new one.

generation-output: changed TODO items resolved: GEN.1423

[8.0.3725] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The deep ice layer of an ice giant is superionic, an ionic fluid or an ice by a measured table of pressure and temperature, not by a single pressure.

Changed

  • Superionic water and ammonia come from a boundary table (GEN.1422). physics/superionic.py reads physics/data/superionic_boundary.json (floors and ceilings of water from the diamond-cell work [R5181] and the shock work [R3081], ammonia and the metallic limits from [R5172]). The ice mantle of an ice giant takes its state, and its water becomes superionic ice, from the pressure and the temperature of the structure model's adiabat at its bottom; the single 100 GPa line is gone, and the weird-worlds line G4 is built for the superionic part. Stand-ins SI1 to SI4 are in section 6.234. This changes ice-giant layer states and materials, so it takes a generator epoch (the Train Manager assigns it).

[8.0.3724] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The solid material beyond a star's snow line is now set by the disk's own condensation budget (a jump of 1.97 times the rock instead of 2.17), with the gas-giant tuning moved so giants stay as common as the surveys find them.

Changed

  • GEN.1396: the jump of the solid surface density at the snow line, which sets the core mass of every planet beyond it (the isolation mass goes as the density to the 3/2), is disk_condensation.SNOW_LINE_SOLID_JUMP (1.967 for the Sun: the rock, the water, ammonia and other ices, and the refractory carbon grains standing at the middle of the water and ammonia lines, over the rock). It replaces the water-only boost of 2.17 in condensate_shares (WATER_ICE_SOLID_BOOST, ice_over_rock and solid_boost are gone). The divisor is the rock alone because the minimum-mass nebula's 7.0 g/cm^2 counts only the silicates and metal; the 1.52 that rock plus grains would give is kept in the notes (stand-ins SSJ1 and SSJ2 in section 6.233). The icy dwarf planets of the Kuiper belt hold about 0.7 rock by mass, above the 0.51 the jump leaves, which is the direction a body that loses ice and cannot gain it should differ.
  • Because the cores beyond the snow line are lighter, GIANT_GAS_SURVIVAL_SHARE goes from 0.766 to 0.79 and GIANT_CORE_CRITICAL_MASS_EARTH from 10 to 9 (inside the 5 to 20 Earth masses the core accretion papers give); over 20,000 Sun-like stars the giants at 2 to 8 AU stay at 0.1065, the hot Jupiters of Sun-like stars go from 0.0058 to 0.0067 and those of M dwarfs from 0.0032 to 0.0034 (the bands are 0.0062 and 0.0027).
  • Generated systems change: every planet beyond its star's snow line has a different core mass (about 0.86 times the old at the same draws), and a few more or fewer giants and ice giants form.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.3723] - 2026-11-08

Headline: Every planet, moon and rogue planet now carries an isotope record: the shares of each isotope of each element it holds, with deuterium, carbon-13, nitrogen-15, argon-40 and the decaying potassium and uranium following physical laws, and the record shown on the property sheet (GEN.1377, GEN.1420 part 1).

Changed

  • New physics/isotope_record.py builds the record from the body's stored composition on its own streams: the table's natural mix by default and, for hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen and argon, a law of the star's metals and age and of the temperature the ice formed at (D/H from the primordial value less the deuterium star formation burned, enriched in ice as the temperature falls, fitted to the ocean and comet 67P; 12C/13C and 14N/15N from the galactic gradients; 36Ar/38Ar from the solar wind; 40Ar from the potassium that decayed and the interior let out). Potassium and uranium isotopes are those of the body's age.
  • Schema v235 (migration 0235): the child tables planet_isotopes, moon_isotopes and rogue_planet_isotopes. A body saved before it has no record and nothing is backfilled.
  • The property sheet of a planet or moon lists the ratios the record moves and the count of isotopes. bulk_draw.formation_temperature_k is now public.
  • Stand-in section 6.236 (ISO1 to ISO9) in the registry, design note composition/isotope-record.md, citations R5173 to R5179.
  • The short-lived isotopes and the cosmogenic ones (GEN.1377, GEN.1421) are the second part.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.3722] - 2026-11-08

Headline: A tilted close-in planet with a thick hydrogen envelope is now puffed up by its obliquity tides, so super-puffs can stay inflated past 1 Gyr.

Changed

  • A planet with an envelope, light above 20 Earth fluxes, a tilt of 0.01 degrees or more and enough tidal power against its starlight has its radius multiplied by the obliquity-tide inflation of [R3079] (up to a factor of 2), from its own tilt and a tidal quality drawn per planet (1e3 to 1e5, log-uniform). A planet the tides have brought to an upright or synchronous state has no tilt to speak of and is not inflated. The planet's tilt is only known after its spin is made, so the inflation is applied in the settle pass.
  • A super-puff is typed by mass, period and density (under 0.1 g/cc) at any age; the age of 1 Gyr is gone from the gate.
  • Stand-in PF5 (the tidal quality range) is registered (GEN.725), PF1 and PF4 are updated.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.3721] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The carbon dioxide of a world whose life makes oxygen is balanced again at the temperature the oxygen leaves it at.

Changed

  • The sink that holds a world's carbon dioxide (continental weathering, seafloor weathering, or a sealed ocean's chemistry) was solved once, at the temperature of the air before life. When oxygenic life burned the air's methane and hydrogen, the air cooled by 7 to 67 K in the worlds measured, and the carbon dioxide stayed as it was, plus the burnt methane. The sink is now asked again at the new temperature, and the carbon dioxide and the temperature are worked against each other until they settle. On 800 systems asked for a habitable world (2,704 bodies) 8 bodies change; one sea world with 35.5 kPa of oxygen goes from 8.4 to 0.8 kPa of carbon dioxide and one body becomes class O.
  • Nothing changes for a world without oxygen, without a carbon sink, or whose air the oddity rows replaced.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.3720] - 2026-11-08

Headline: Every job of the work queue now takes a claim on the host's memory and load before it starts, so a generation run no longer takes the machine down.

Added

  • One memory and load gate for all jobs (PERF.254, queue/memorygate.py, queue/claims.py). A worker takes a claim (memory in MB, cores, lane) for each job before it prepares it and waits, with its heartbeat going, until the host has room: the free memory from the kernel's MemAvailable (and a cgroup limit when there is one), less a reserve for MySQL, Redis and the web server, less the places kept for the interactive and long lanes, less the part of every other claim not yet in memory (read from the proportional memory of each worker and its horse, psutil 7.2.2, a new dependency in both lock files). Cores are claimed the same way and an ordinary job waits while the one-minute load per core is over 1.25. The wait is bounded (300 s) and then the old table cap decides, so a wrong gate cannot stall a run. Every kind of job has a claim (a run's units, the API's and the pages' jobs, the Generate page's, the node prefetch, the cut of a stage) and tests/test_memory_gate.py fails for a kind that has none. The test runner takes a claim for each phase.
  • Claims are learned. The worker's heartbeat samples what the job's processes hold; the largest peak seen for a kind is claimed, with 10 percent on top, in place of the table's figure when it is larger.
  • A job killed for memory is retried once with a larger claim, then the run stops with the unit (or the opening) named and what it claimed and held.

Changed

  • The cut of a stage is a job of its own (units.open_stage, claimed alone on the bulk lane) and no longer runs inside the work horse of the last unit of the stage before; a failure or a kill there is filed under its own stage. Cancel, Clear and the update guard know the job.
  • scripts/test.py runs each phase under a claim on the gate when a Redis server answers.
  • Generated output is unchanged.

[8.0.3719] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The life and air history API test draws the same systems every run, so it no longer fails now and then.

Changed

  • The life and air history test is seeded (TEST.709). Its helper drew up to forty unseeded systems to find an airy rocky planet, and about one run in five came out with a planet whose air history has no methane row. Each attempt now draws on a stream of its own, so every run reads the same planet. Only test code changes; it passed 50 runs in a row.

generation-output: unchanged

[8.0.3718] - 2026-11-08

Headline: a script that measures how far each class quantity moves when one stand-in is moved across its registered range.

Changed

  • scripts/stand_in_sensitivity.py (GEN.1311, part one of the class fudge table): reads the registry's constant and knobs cells, overrides one module constant at a time (low end, high end) on a fixed sample of systems, and records how far gravity, mean temperature, pressure, gas shares, ocean cover, the regional, day and night temperatures and the wet bulb move. rows lists which registry rows can be overridden and why the others cannot; screen runs the pass and writes a report. Nothing it does changes a generated world.

[8.0.3717] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The registry now keeps eighteen known gaps from the unseen-compounds report as watch lines, each with its status, its chance of existing, its chance that the predicted properties are right, and why it changes no generated number yet.

Added

  • docs/design/research/stand-in-values.md section 6.238 lists the watch lines: solid metallic hydrogen, sulfide and salt clouds, ices beyond ice X, the Mercury hollows phase, Titan cryominerals, superionic iron alloys, Venus heavy-metal frost, tholins, bcc iron, Fe-Si-O phases, noble-gas compounds, doubly superionic ammonia-water, post-post-perovskite, phosphine on Venus, dimethyl sulfide on K2-18 b, quark cores, azotosomes and superheavy nuclides.
  • Each line has a status in evidence-register.md: predicted only, disputed (solid metallic hydrogen, phosphine, dimethyl sulfide) or observed in a lab (the Titan co-crystals). Fifteen papers join the references.

[8.0.3716] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The list of stand-in values now says for every row whether the thing it stands for has been seen: in a planet, in a laboratory, predicted only, or disputed. Seven materials that were once only predicted are now ordinary seen rows.

Added

  • docs/design/research/stand-in-values.md has an evidence-status column, filled from docs/design/research/evidence-register.md; a row with no line there reads predicted only, and a test fails if any row has no status. A short note beside the tier explains the four statuses.

[8.0.3713] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The chemistry the one measured acid cloud holds is now a registered set that the generator can give to any air with the supplies for it.

Added

  • The sulfur-cloud chemistry set V1 to V10 and its six gates (GEN.1425, part A). physics/sulfur_cloud_set.py and physics/data/sulfur_cloud_set.json hold the acid droplets, the sulfur gases, the lower sulfur oxides, sulfur aerosol, the chlorine and iron compounds and the measured ultraviolet-absorber band as stand-ins with tier, tweak and evidence status, and chemistry(values) says which of them an air gets: sulfur in an oxidising air, an acid cloud by the vapor curve of GEN.1424, reduced sulfur from the star's ultraviolet-C, chlorine, and iron and carbon supply. A hot volcanic carbon-dioxide world under a bright star gets V1 to V5 (and V6, V7 and V10 where chlorine and exposed iron are present), a cold sulfur-poor world gets none, and V8 and V9 are off by default. Nothing is stored yet; the cloud step reads it in part B.

[8.0.3712] - 2026-11-08

Headline: The one-line description of a planet class and its class-page sentence now live in one row, with no number typed by hand and no Solar System feature stated as a fact of the class.

Changed

  • GEN.1432: each row of planet_classes.json now holds the class's phrase (what a planet or moon page says after "It is") beside its page sentence; planet_class_text.json is gone and planet_class_text.py reads the phrase from the class rows. The two had disagreed for about ten of the 25 letters (class A said "small, barren" though it asks for sulfur dioxide in the air; class F said "volcanic with shallow seas" though it asks for an air with almost no oxygen). A body's brine is built from the cations of the crust it weathers (the melt of its mantle, with sodium and potassium put back because the stored rock carries no alkalis) and the anions of its ocean class (neutral, soda, chloride brine, acid sulfate). Its ions go to salts in the order of the chemical divides: jarosite and alunite (acid water), calcite, the alkaline path (magnesium carbonate, then nahcolite, trona, thermonatrite or natrite), the calcium path (gypsum or anhydrite, epsomite, hexahydrite or kieserite, mirabilite or thenardite, calcium chloride), perchlorate in thin oxidizing air, then halite, carnallite, sylvite, bischofite and antarcticite. Gypsum or anhydrite follows Hardie's measured equilibrium of temperature and water activity (R5164), so a halite-saturated brine makes anhydrite above about 18 degrees C. The other hydrate boundaries and the ion budget are registered stand-ins (section 6.226, rows EV1 to EV11).

[8.0.3635] - 2026-11-08

Headline: A planet's tide can no longer spend more energy than its orbit has to give: a strong tide wears the eccentricity down as it heats the planet.

Changed

  • The eccentricity falls at the rate the tide really takes the orbit's energy (GEN.1351). A planet's eccentricity was worn down by the tide with the body's cold rheology (the mantle at the temperature the star's age gives it with no tide), while the heat it was given was worked out with the mantle the tide itself warms, and in the extreme melts. A 0.0013 Earth-mass planet at 0.0134 AU round a 0.09 solar-mass star kept e = 0.068 over 1.8 Gyr (a cold circularisation time of 18 Gyr) with a tide of 33 W/m2 that would circularise it in 27 Myr, spending 2.4e31 J against an orbital energy of 2.3e31 J when circularising releases about 1e29 J. The orbit now loses the tide's power as its eccentricity falls (E_orb d(e^2)/dt = -P, E_orb = G M m / (2 a)), with P the heat model's tide at that eccentricity (interior_heat.eccentricity_tide_w, the box for a rocky body, the shell for an icy one), integrated from the birth eccentricity over the star's age (orbit_elements.settled_eccentricity). The sample body now ends at e = 0.019 with a tide of 7e10 W; the energy a tide held at its end power for the whole age spends never passes the orbit's E_orb (e_birth^2 - e^2). A weak tide changes nothing (the heat model's decay time is then the cold one); only planets and captured moons whose tide melts or softens their mantle end on a lower eccentricity, and with it a smaller tidal heat flux. The grid of the integration is registered in GEN.725 (OE16, numerical settings). Generated eccentricities, tidal heat flux and what follows from them (climate, class, life) change for the planets on the tight orbits of small stars; the census of tidal heat flux is re-measured at the lock.

Headline: The mass a giant takes out of an outer disk now arrives where it went: thrown-out bodies heavy enough to be rogue planets, the implant of an inner belt, and the moons the planets catch.

Changed

  • Where an outer disk's lost mass goes (GEN.1308). The mass an outer disk lost to its giant (what the giant cleared around its orbit and what its move scattered) is shared by the scatter step's rules (the ejected share from the giant's Safronov number, the rest by the swept split) and handed on. The ejected part goes to the rogue builders: the bodies of it that are heavy enough to be rogue planets by the disk's size law are built as rogues of that system (a disk of small bodies throws out no planet, only debris). The implanted part goes whole to the inner belt nearest the disk's inner edge, which grows by it and says so on its page; a disk with no inner belt loses it. The captured part is what the planets' irregular moons are caught from first, and the disk's own mass falls only for what they hold above it. The disk's own mass is not lowered again. Belts that receive an implant, and the rogues of a disk, change the generation of the systems that have them.

Changed

  • physics/oddities.py gains apply(body, levers): it asks the table for the rows whose gate holds for the body (quantities_of), rolls each on its own stream keyed by the star, orbit and mass (body_key, no draw from the run's stream), runs the effect the row names (EFFECTS, filled by register), and records the ids on body.oddities. The planet build calls it for the bulk inputs (lever L3) right after the composition is drawn; later wiring items call it at their own steps.
  • SystemConfig.FORCE_ODDITIES forces rows whose gate holds (a body still cannot be given what its conditions forbid) and SystemConfig.WEIRDNESS_DIAL sets a run's own dial; the tuning dial applies when a run has none, and 0 turns every oddity off.
  • planets, moons and rogue_planets gain oddities (VARCHAR(40), comma separated ids, NULL for none): schema v226, migration 0226 (number provisional), stored and loaded with the body.

  • Oddity W10 (GEN.1048, iron-rich core) is wired: the planet architecture's merger count reaches the planet (collision_count), and a rocky planet under 10 Earth masses with a merger can have lost much of its mantle to a giant impact (about 1 in 20): it keeps its mass, its iron share rises (physics/mantle_stripping.py, strip_mantle), its water goes with the mantle, and its radius and density follow. The energy ratio of the impact is a new stand-in (MT8, tweak L3, burn-down line added).
  • Oddity W2 (GEN.1048, Venus-type spin) is wired: a rocky planet with an air of 10 bar or more and no large moon, whose star's tide on its air has had the time to balance the solid tide, turns slowly backwards like Venus when it was born tilted past the split angle (physics/venus_spin.py; a day of 20 days or more, the axis upside down). The effect declines a planet whose end state is prograde, so the page names only the real ones. The spin lever is rolled again each time a planet's spin is made again (new air, new moons, new age), so the label always matches the body.
  • Oddity W1 (GEN.1048, extreme tilt seasons) is named for a rocky planet tilted 60 to 120 degrees with no large moon; the tilt was already drawn and the seasonal temperatures already read it, so only the page and API gain the label.
  • Oddities W3, W4 and W5 (GEN.1049) are wired. W5: the periods of a star's planets are searched for resonant chains once the orbits are final, and about a fifth of the planets in a chain (WR8) are held on the eccentricity their neighbours force on them (0.001 and up); the star's tide then flexes them, so their interior heat, air and class are made again (planets.finish_orbit_oddities). W3: an orbit of eccentricity 0.5 or more is named on the page (the eccentricity law is unchanged; the census compares its tail with the literature). W4: a giant closer than 10 stellar radii has a chance by host temperature (8, 63 and 80 percent under 6,250 K, to 7,000 K and above) of a polar orbit, its inclination drawn from the measured peak of 80 to 125 degrees.
  • Oddities W14 and W9 (GEN.1050) are wired. W14: a rocky planet under 0.11 Earth mass with a period under a day and a dayside over 2,000 K is named a disintegrating planet when its wind has not already used it up over the star's age (physics/disintegrating_planet.py; the body is not changed). W9: a planet or giant whose ring came from a moon the tide pulled inside the Roche limit (the moon history of GEN.1057, which already made the ring) is named for it on the page.
  • Oddities W19 and W20 (GEN.1051) are wired (physics/air_branches.py). The air solver now reads the planet's own history: after it settles, a planet whose air has two stable states (the cold-start and warm-start solutions differ by 20 K and more than 0.1 in ice cover, a dayside under 330 K) may take the other branch (W20, half of those that have one), and a tidally locked planet whose nightside is cold enough to freeze its main gas out may lose its air to the nightside cap (W19, nightside_collapse); the lost air is the airless state, the night-side cap and its residual pressure are not stored. Neither draws from the run stream, so a world without these oddities is unchanged.
  • Oddity G1 (GEN.1058) is wired: an ice giant of 5 to 30 Earth masses that the merger of giant_tilt.tilt_after_merger_deg left tipped 60 degrees or more (Uranus's 98) is named on the page as tipped by an impact.   • A work unit of Boss's warm-up (unit 11) ended with status 15 (SIGTERM), and nothing in the program sends that to a work horse (OPS.118). The usual sender is a memory guard on the host: earlyoom and systemd-oomd end the biggest process with SIGTERM when memory runs low, before the kernel's own killer would end it with SIGKILL, and a work unit of the warm-up is often the biggest. The cause on the test server cannot be named from the program; the next occurrence is in error.log (OPS.116) with its signal, unit and run.

[8.0.3606] - 2026-11-07

Headline: Two warm-ups never run at the same time: the update's warm-up has priority and cancels any other, a change's warm-up waits, one started by hand refuses; the phase lines give the time the phase took.

Fixed

  • update.sh's warm-up part 2 failed with run ... is running when the epoch's warm-up had started the moment the update ended (OPS.117). The update's own warm-up now has priority: it cancels any other cache warm-up that holds the machine (the epoch's, the one after an orbital update, one started by hand) through the normal cancel path, waits for the canceled run's units to stop, and goes on. The canceled warm-up ends with one plain line, not as a failure.
  • A warm-up that is not the update's never starts while another runs. The one a change starts waits for the running one to end (nothing written to the phase record meanwhile) and then warms what is left; one started by hand says which run holds the machine and exits without starting.
  • A canceled warm-up could write into the phase record of the run after it. The record belongs to the run that began it; late writes from any other process are dropped, so the admin page never shows two runs at once.
  • The Phase N of 5 lines added up the units' own seconds (5338 s for a phase that took 9:39 with nine chunks at once). They now give the time the phase took; the admin page keeps the worker seconds as worker_seconds.
  • The phenomena line said chunks of up to 8,543,000 phenomena because the first slice's share of the objects the cap leaves out was counted into the chunk size. A slice now reports its own size.
  • A work unit whose process was ended by SIGTERM was reported as a probable out-of-memory kill. The failure now names the signal: SIGKILL is the kernel's out-of-memory killer, SIGTERM is something asking the process to end.

Headline: One file, error.log in the log folder, now records every error and crash from everything, while each error still goes to its own log too.

Changed

  • error.log (beside warmup.log and the others, logpaths.error_log_path) holds every line of severity error and critical that any logger writes, the program's or another library's (OPS.116). A line is in the display form with the fields log= (the log the error also went to: warmup.log, tiles.log, orbits.log, update.log, apache for the web app, else console) and pid=, and a traceback follows its line. It is made on the first error, mode 0660, by the one logging module (util/log.py); the setup scripts make it for the web server's user, the folder's rotation rule (*.log) covers it, and the macOS rotation file names it.
  • Crashes: an uncaught exception in the main thread or another is written as critical with its traceback whether or not the debug log is on, and a fatal signal in a library (SIGSEGV and the like) leaves the interpreter's dump of every thread in the file. A Ctrl+C is not an error.
  • Killed or crashed processes are written by their parent: a detached worker (exit status or signal), a work horse the out-of-memory killer or kill -9 ended (units.horse_killed, for any job, not only a run's unit), a job a dead worker left running (reap_dead_jobs), a web job's step that exited non-zero and a one-off command that failed, timed out or did not start, each with the last error lines the program printed. A detached worker stopped on purpose (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) and an update's refusal are not errors; a work horse ended by SIGTERM is written, with its signal and unit, because RQ only calls the handler for an end nobody asked for (the case of Boss's warm-up, unit 11, status 15).
  • The web app writes an unhandled exception with its route and traceback, and any other 5xx answer with its route, once; the deliberate 503 of a closed site or a cache being rebuilt is not an error.
  • update.sh and install.sh write every error they print to the file too, name the command that made them stop with its exit status and the step, and a warm-up stage that does not finish is written there though the screen only warns.
  • docs/design/operations/logging-standard.md has an "The error log" section, docs/reference/logging.md lists the file, and log_dir's help names it. src/tests/test_error_log.py holds one test per source.

Headline: The life of a harsh world can now be tougher than the life of an easy one: a world with a lot of radiation, hydrogen sulfide or carbon dioxide may carry an "adapted to" trait, and microbes now stand a thousand times the radiation an animal does.

Changed

  • GEN.876, adaptation traits. A body's life draws up to three traits, one for each stress the life scores have a limit to widen: radiation, hydrogen sulfide and carbon dioxide (physics/adaptation_traits.py, physics/adaptation_draw.py). A trait is tolerant (grade 2) or extreme (grade 3). The chance of a trait is 0.8 times a stress score that rises with the logarithm of the stress from the ordinary limit to the extreme grade's, and a share of them equal to half the stress score squared are extreme. [8.0.3557] - 2026-11-07

Headline: A New galaxy job no longer waits for ever on a generation run that nothing follows any more: a run left behind by a process that is still running is freed, and a run whose set-up fails ends instead of holding the machine.

Changed

  • A run nobody follows is freed, even when its process is still running (ADM.136). The run line freed a holder only when its process id was gone, or, for a run on another host, when its alive key had run out. A run left behind by a process that lives on (a worker that stays up, or a process id the system reused) counted as live for ever, so a New galaxy job that came after it waited behind it until its time ran out. A run now counts as dead when its record is over, when its process id is gone, or when its alive key has run out, which a followed run never lets happen.
  • A followed run keeps its alive key while its follower is busy (ADM.136). The follower said so only at each poll, so a callback that took longer than two minutes (saving what a stage found) would have let the key run out and the run look dead. The process that follows a run now says so from a thread of its own every 30 seconds until the run ends.
  • A run whose set-up fails ends as failed (ADM.136). The set-up after the machine is taken (making sure workers run, the debug relay, the run's log) was outside the block that ends the run on an error, so a failure there left the run live for a process that went on; the next run waited for it.
  • src/tests/test_run_control.py (found on the way): test_a_started_unit_is_sent_the_stop_command passed the fetched job object to queue.remove, which does not take it for a job when the queue's job class differs from the fetched one; it passes the id.

  • DB.114: every writer of the bright-star and phenomenon scatter tables now runs the Object ID step inside a transaction that is retried. After DB.113 fixed the scatter units, the sector backfills (by luminosity and by mass), the special phenomena write and each batch of the sky charting still ran the same ID step with other writes in the same transaction and no retry, so a deadlock (MySQL error 1213) or lock wait timeout (1205) with other workers stopped the run. Each of them is now one whole transaction at READ COMMITTED (the sector locks, the draw, the stars with their IDs, the levels and the ledger) that db.contention.run_with_retries rolls back and writes again, with the same waits, logging and exclusive grant after the eighth failed try as DB.113. The stars written are the ones an undisturbed run writes, and a progress tick is not given twice.

[8.0.3525] - 2026-11-07

Headline: A queue worker now runs only the functions the program queues, so a process that can write to Redis cannot get a worker to call an arbitrary function.

Changed

  • SEC.45: a fixed list of the functions a queued job may name (planetgen/queue/allowlist.py). A job in Redis names the function a worker calls; with pickle gone (SEC.39) the name was still data, so anything that could write to Redis could name any function a worker could import. Every queue now builds its jobs with GuardedJob and every worker reads them with it: the function a job names, and its success, failure and stopped callbacks, must be on FUNCTIONS (a run's unit and its failure callback, the dependency callbacks, the API dispatcher api_jobs.execute, the Generate page's job_runner.run, the node prefetch). A job that names anything else is logged as refused and fails in the failed registry with the reason; nothing runs. api_jobs.execute is itself a dispatcher (it calls the function in its first argument), so what it may call is a second fixed list, API_FUNCTIONS (the API's edit, generate, gravity and page-answer jobs, and run_command). A test sweeps the source and fails when a place that queues work names a function that is not on the lists.
  • A worker's environment variable PLANETGEN_QUEUE_EXTRA_FUNCTIONS (module:name or module:*, comma separated) adds functions; it is unset in production and the test suite sets it for the plain functions its queue tests run. The arguments of an allowed function are not checked: run_command still runs the command line it is given, so the Redis ACL user and password (examples/redis/planetgen-acl.conf) stay the wall that keeps other processes out.

Changed

  • src/planetgen/util/detmath.py (PERF.246): matmul of a product too large to form at once (more than _ACCUMULATE_LIMIT products) went through a loop of inner array operations. [8.0.3498] - 2026-11-07

Headline: A MySQL deadlock between two scatter workers no longer stops the massive-star stage.

Fixed

  • DB.113: the massive-star scatter died with "Deadlock found when trying to get lock" (error 1213) on a run with 15 workers. Each worker's batch of stars gives the new rows their Object IDs (scatter_uids.assign), which reads every row of the table that has no ID yet, so workers writing at once met on each other's uncommitted rows. A batch of the massive-star, bright-star-band and phenomenon scatters now runs at READ COMMITTED and starts over (up to 8 tries, with a short pause) after a deadlock or lock wait timeout; the retry writes the same rows with the same IDs.
  • Retries wait longer when there is more trouble, and ask for the step to themselves at the end. New db/contention.py: each retry waits a random, growing time (longer when this process has failed lately, capped at 5 s). After the 8th failed try the unit raises a need for exclusive use of the step; the system grants it with a MySQL named lock that the other writers of the same step check before each try, so they hold off, and the unit tries once more alone. Every retry (error and wait), need, grant, hold-off and release is logged.

[8.0.3447] - 2026-11-06

Headline: Every log line says where it is with one of three words, Stage, Part or Phase, and every line names its component from one table.

Changed

  • A count is worded in one place (OPS.103): Stage N of M for the top-level steps of an update, an install or a generate job, Part N of M for the runs inside one (the update's two warm-up runs), and Phase N of M for a named group inside a run (the warm-up's phases). The warm-up's families are named, and its progress counts them as family 2 of 2. chunk is only ever a count of pieces of work. update.sh words the warm-up runs part 1 of 2 and part 2 of 2 (they were stage 1 and stage 2, which collided with the update's own stages), the queue page and the cluster-field messages use the same wording, and the update guard's failed step reads stage 4 of 9, checking the generator's math, set by log_stage itself.
  • The component of a record is one of the names in logrecord.COMPONENTS and nothing else (update, install, warm, tiles, orbits, generate, queue, web, job, activity, command, lib, logs, permissions, cache-dir, swap, python-deps). Record refuses another name, logrecord.component_of finds the one a logger or a source file belongs to, and the shell scripts take their list from the same table. The queue run page's records now say queue (they said run), and a library's own log lines say lib.

A locked world, a world that turns backwards, a 28-day spinner near resonance and Earth all come out of the same formula; an optional transmission (the ring's shade) multiplies the light where the star is up.

[8.0.3417] - 2026-11-06

Headline: Every body's bands now show the longest day and night it really has: Nitrikin III's equator reads about a week of unbroken day, not nothing.

Changed

  • The longest unbroken day and night of each latitude band were the polar day alone, worked out from a closed form that is 0 at every latitude without a polar circle. A body that turns once in 27.9 days round a 28.5-day orbit has a solar day of 14.1 days and a sun that rises and sets while its declination moves, so its equator read 0 where the real longest daylight is about 7 days. One search now serves every body: it steps the star through the year and the turns of the planet from the body's own spin, orbit, tilt, star size and solar day, and reads the longest run above (or below) the horizon. Nitrikin III's equator comes out at 7.1 days, its tropics at 8.4 days, its middle latitudes at about 17 days and its pole at 14.25 days. Earth's pole reads 184 days of day and 181 of night, and its equator half a day. A band whose stretch outlasts a solar day reads as polar day and night (GEN.1260).
  • The Day and Night rows were the year's average share of the turn the star is up, times the solar day, which reads half a solar day at every latitude. They are now the mean length of a day and of a night from the same search (the time the star is up, or down, over the number of separate stretches), and are labelled "Mean day" and "Mean night": Nitrikin III's equator band reads about 7 days of each, its polar band about 10 days, and Earth's equator 12 hours.
  • Only stored values change; no draw is added or removed.

The cut on the dust is a stand-in tuned so the K, G and F dwarfs together hold a disk about as often as the surveys find (about 17 percent); Sun-like stars come out near 8 percent (survey 14), the A stars have none (survey 24) and the F stars about half their share, gaps that come from the outer disk's mass and width and are registered with the cut (DU1). Stars whose planets are not built (no planets asked for, a pulsar, a planetary-nebula pair) have no disk.

[8.0.3380] - 2026-11-06

Headline: A test that hangs past its time limit is now stopped, named and reported, and the test run goes on instead of waiting for hours.

Fixed

  • The full non-browser run hung twice with every worker idle (1.5 h and 3 h). pytest-timeout's signal fires once and raises in the test; a test that holds a process pool then waits for its children as the with block closes (shutdown(wait=True)), and a child that is still busy never ends, so the alarm was spent and nothing stopped the wait. Reproduced with a two-child pool that sleeps.
  • New tests/hang_guard.py (loaded from pytest.ini): a second clock on a thread of its own for every test, over setup, call and teardown. Past the test's limit plus hang_guard_grace (120 s) it prints HUNG TEST <node id> (worker ...) and kills the worker's child processes, so the wait ends and the timeout is reported as the test's failure; 120 s later, if the test is still running, it ends the worker (os._exit(70)), which xdist reports as a crashed worker on that test and replaces.
  • scripts/test.py stops a phase that prints nothing for two hours (PLANETGEN_TEST_IDLE_LIMIT_S, 0 turns it off), says HUNG RUN, and returns exit code 124.

Added

  • tests/test_hang_guard.py (a hung pool is killed and the next test runs; a test stuck on nothing a child can end loses its worker under xdist and the run goes on; no limit, no watch; the process-tree helpers) and three tests of the idle limit in tests/test_test_runner.py.

[8.0.3378] - 2026-11-05

Headline: The dust that dims a galaxy's stars can now be worked out from the galaxy's own gas, so a small galaxy no longer inherits the Milky Way's dust.

Changed

  • physics/dust_model.py (VIEW.43) works out the dust of a galaxy from the gas of every ring of its disk (GEN.469), the metals of that gas (GEN.1269 and the dust-to-gas law of [R5102]) and the thickness a gas layer has in the disk's own gravity. It gives two tables, the extinction through the whole layer and the layer's scale height, against radius. The extinction per parsec is the column over twice the height times sech squared of the height above the plane. One constant comes from a measurement (2.21e21 hydrogen atoms per magnitude, [R5130]) and one is tuned (a half of the gas column dims the stars a catalogue can use).
  • In a galaxy shaped like the Milky Way it gives 1.06 magnitudes a kpc in the plane at the Sun and 0.24 magnitudes through the layer, and about 39 magnitudes from the Sun to the Galactic Center; the fixed law gave 2.3. A galaxy of the test galaxy's size gives 0.14 magnitudes a kpc where the fixed law gave 9.6.
  • sky_photometry.dust_av_per_pc takes the table form (profile=) beside the fixed law; av_per_kpc_at_sun=0 still means no dust. Nothing reads the profile yet: the sky route, the glow band and the tier ledger take it in VIEW.44, so the sky is unchanged by this note.
  • Five stand-in rows, DU1 to DU5 (section 6.188 of the registry), and five references ([R5130] to [R5134]).

The copy is checked first (whole records only), the galaxy database is reached before anything is changed, and the restore is refused at once, before the safety archive is taken, while a save is writing parity. The file is written beside the live one, synced, and renamed over it with the live file locked.
  • The restored file is then checked against the database (db/parity.reconcile, the check of DB.8 with the stale-record rule of DB.9): a record that no longer matches the rows because the database changed after the backup is made again from the rows and is not read as damage; a record that fails its CRC is made again when the sector verifies; a member whose sector is gone is let go. The result says how many sectors the copy holds no record of (unprotected until their next save or planetgen refresh-parity) and lists the sectors that are damaged or cannot be trusted, for planetgen repair-db.
  • A backup part may now refuse a restore before anything is changed (Part.check_restorable), and RestoreContext.database names the galaxy database a part checks against; ParityFile.locked(wait=False) raises ParityFileBusy instead of waiting.

Headline: The habitability re-score no longer dies with a MySQL deadlock when four workers run its units at once.

Fixed

  • rescore-habitability ran each unit as one transaction at the default isolation level, so two workers re-scoring neighbouring id ranges held gap locks on the shared system_interests and planet index ranges and each waited on the other (MySQL error 1213), which stopped the stage. The unit now runs at READ COMMITTED, which takes no gap locks, and starts over on a deadlock or a lock wait timeout (store.RETRYABLE_ERRORS) on a connection of its own, up to store.SECTOR_SAVE_ATTEMPTS times (8) with a pause that grows with each try, then fails as before. The numbers are the same whenever a unit is run, so a retry changes nothing stored.

Added

  • tests/test_perf228_rescore_deadlock.py: four threads re-scoring neighbouring ranges of 16 saved systems for 12 rounds each finish with no error (it failed on the old unit with error 1213), a unit that meets one deadlock gives the same answer, a unit that keeps meeting one gives up after 8 attempts, and any other database error is not retried.

The course's stops (the two ends and any systems between them on the route) are placed in the galaxy frame from the sector's center, so the map draws the route, the straight line, any bend round a keep-out sphere, the rings, the names and the course readout and diagram, as it does for a course across the galaxy.

Added

  • planetgen warm --follow draws the progress of the warm-up that is running, started by update.sh or by hand, from its run record in Redis, the same bars and phase lines the starting session shows. It starts nothing; ending it with Ctrl+C or a hangup leaves the warm-up running. It says so when none is running.

[8.0.3352] - 2026-11-05

Headline: A full backup now holds a copy of the sector repair file, so a galaxy whose live repair file is lost can still be repaired.

Changed

  • New backup part parity (DB.40, backup/parts.py): a copy of the parity file of the database repair (db/parity_file.py, DB.9) in parity/sector-parity.pgpr. The copy is taken with the file locked against every save (the lock the saves take) and cut at the end of its last whole record, so it is a state the file really had, never half a record. A file damaged behind its last record is refused with the reason (run planetgen repair-db), because that copy could repair nothing. With no parity file yet the part is empty and says so.
  • The manifest keeps what a part says about its dump as info (Part.dump may return a dict); for the parity part it is bytes, sectors covered and groups, or present: false with the reason. planetgen.backup.PartInfo.info holds it.
  • New option settings.backup_parity (default on, Admin settings, "Back up the repair file"): off leaves the copy out of full archives, for a very large galaxy. The settings backup made before each save still holds the settings part alone.
  • Restoring the part is DB.41; until then a restore of a whole archive leaves the parity copy in the archive and says so.

Fixed

Two passes on two threads overlapped: the one that finished first put the chance back to 1 in 1,000 under the one still running, which made no species, and the one that finished last saved the first one's value of 1 and left the chance there for every test after it. That is why test_two_passes_drawing_the_same_names_still_save_unique_ones failed alone and passed in a whole-file run. The first block in saves the chance and the last one out puts it back, under a lock.

[8.0.3299] - 2026-11-05

Headline: An ice giant can now radiate as little heat as Uranus does, or as much as Neptune does, instead of every one of them getting Neptune's.

Changed

  • GEN.1033: the spread of ice-giant internal heat. The cooling law runs through Jupiter and Neptune, so a Uranus-mass giant got Neptune's 0.32 W/m2 where Uranus radiates 0.042 W/m2 (Neptune 0.433). An ice giant now has one of two interiors: mixed (the law as it was) or layered by a stable compositional gradient that stops the convection and leaves a thermal boundary layer, radiating 3 to 30 percent of the law (log-uniform; 0.01 to 0.095 W/m2 at Uranus's mass, inside its measured 0.042 +0.047 -0.042). The chance of a layered interior is one half, from one of the two measured ice giants having one. The cause is the one the thermal evolution models give (a gradient is needed because no adiabatic interior reproduces Uranus's luminosity) and the impact history that mixes or spares it; sources are in the registry (R5115 to R5120, added to the References). The draw is on a stream of the giant's own (its mass), so the one-bar temperature, the helium rain, the air and the habitability all read the same heat and the run's stream does not move. Gas giants, brown dwarfs and rocky bodies are untouched. Stand-ins registered in GEN.725: IGH1 (T4, L0), IGH2 (T2, L1), IGH3 (T6, L0). The row CC14 (the Uranus anomaly of the old law) is retired.

[8.0.3266] - 2026-11-05

Headline: The star backfill can now draw a whole sphere of space by blocks instead of cell by cell, giving the same stars much faster for the far bright bands, and the sky tier table reaches faint stars near the observer.

Changed

  • bright_stars.backfill_sphere and backfill_mass_sphere (VIEW.41) draw every cell whose centre lies within a radius, by the blocks of backfill_cells and backfill_mass_cells: a band on the candidate path is looked up block by block, so a sparse band costs one count per block of 256 cells and one lookup per candidate, and only the cells that hold a star are handed to the cell draw. The stars are exactly the ones the cell draw gives (tests/test_backfill_sphere.py compares them on the candidate path, the cell path and a mix, over a sphere that wraps past longitude 0, one on the core and one on the pole). Measured on a 3,500 parsec sphere the brightest band takes 281 seconds for 2.8 billion cells (reports/system-sky-sphere-draw-2026-11-05.md); VIEW.19 priced the cell draw at 2 to 30 microseconds a cell.
  • spherical.sphere_rows and cell_in_sphere split the walk of enumerate_sectors_within_radius into the rows a sphere crosses with their window of wedges, and the exact test of one cell; the enumeration is built on them and lists the same cells (it may list a row's wedges in another order). bright_stars.bound_terms and bound_of split block_bound into the parts that do not depend on the luminosity band; the bound is the same to the last bit.
  • sky_tiers (VIEW.24) counts a band's cost in block and row visits (block_visits, BLOCK_VISIT_BUDGET 1e8, replacing the cell budget): a dust-free 7.5 sky takes 4.3e7 visits instead of 8.3e9 cell visits, so no band is dropped by default. It adds mass rings under 1 solar mass (NEAR_RING_MASSES_SOL), each drawn as far as RING_MIN_YIELD (1 percent) of its stars still shows, 8 to 62 parsecs at 7.5. Registry rows SKT1, SKT3 to SKT6 (6.176). Nothing reads either yet; the charting step (VIEW.25) will.

[8.0.3245] - 2026-11-05

Headline: A route can now come back with the graph round it: the links between its stops and from each stop to the systems next to it.

Changed

  • nav_between and nav_course take with_graph, and GET /api/nav takes graph=1; the route then has graph: nodes (the linked systems off the route, with their galaxy-frame positions), edges (from, to, distance_ly, on_route) and more (how many linked systems a stop's cap left out). The route's own hops are always edges, on_route true, with the lengths route.hops gives. The other links follow the relative neighbourhood graph rule (Boss's answer 3.2 on the schematic route map): two points are linked when no system lies closer to both than they are to each other. It has no tuning number and gives about 1.5 links to a system. A link is a neighbour relation, not a travel lane.
  • The systems round a stop come from the cell-key index (db/route_neighbours.py, the same covering index the nearby search uses), so no new route search runs and the cost follows the neighbourhood, not the galaxy. Each stop weighs its NAV_GRAPH_CANDIDATES (24) nearest systems and lists at most NAV_GRAPH_NEIGHBOURS (6) off the route. A route in a sector with no galaxy placement takes its neighbours from the sector. Without graph=1 nothing is read and the route is as before.
  • Measured on a synthetic galaxy of 150,000 systems in each of two boxes (about 0.08 systems per cubic parsec, like the Sun's neighbourhood, and about 4 per cubic parsec, a dense region), on the slow lane machine: 5 to 7 ms a stop, so 6 stops took 29 to 36 ms, 20 stops 104 to 116 ms and 60 stops 360 to 384 ms, about a rung and a half of the index per stop. The graph reads the stops' own positions from the same index as their neighbours, because the route search places a system at its sector's centre plus the offset without turning the offset into the galaxy frame (reported as a bug).
  • Tests: the rule against a brute-force graph, the hops, the cap and its more, the on-route flag, the links between two stops, a route inside one sector, a route over two sectors, the nearest-systems reader against brute force, and the API with and without graph=1.

[8.0.3234] - 2026-11-05

Headline: A warm-up with nothing changed no longer visits every object page again: its object phase takes seconds, not minutes.

While a slice of an object family is warmed, the page cache now records the Redis key of every answer its pages read or stored, the counter of each tag they read and the incarnation; the next run reads the counters and checks the keys in two round trips and does not visit a slice whose counters, incarnation and answers all stand. A tag that moved (any change that touches the slice), an answer that left Redis, a page that failed when the slice was first warmed, or a Redis that does not answer visits the slice as before, so the rule for when an answer is stale is the cache's own. The objects phase of an unchanged run on the test galaxy went from 214 s to 4.5 s (10,014 objects, one process). The slice record lives half as long as its answers (page_cache.shared_seconds), so an answer nearing its expiry is looked at again in time.

[8.0.3227] - 2026-11-05

Headline: One command, python3 -m planetgen.cli.tiles, builds the whole Galaxy Map's tile cache from scratch, and a nightly timer runs it after the orbit update.

Changed

  • The whole-map build (PERF.233). planetgen.cli.tiles builds every node of every level of the whole galaxy (a block of each level that holds a generated sector or a placed object, and each generated sector) into a new cache beside the live one and swaps it in when it is complete, so visitors never meet an empty cache and a run that is killed leaves the old cache serving. It builds a level at a time, tile_cache.build_workers processes at once (0 is one per core), prints a line per level, ignores the cache budget while it runs, checks the data once more before the swap and refuses to start unless twice the projected size is free on the cache's disk.
  • cache.max_mb counts only the nodes visits asked for. The nodes built ahead (the build's and the warm-up's) are no longer counted against the budget or pruned, so a full cache no longer makes every on-demand node get deleted at the next prune.
  • A nightly timer. examples/maintenance/planetgen-tiles@.service and .timer run the build at 05:00 after the orbit update, then planetgen warm rebuilds the lists, objects and search; install-maintenance-timer.sh installs and enables them (--skip-tiles-timer leaves them out). Documented in INSTALL.md, docs/reference/cli.md and docs/design/operations/cache-warm-up.md.

The result is the surface brightness in magnitudes per square arcsecond; in a galaxy shaped like the Milky Way it runs from about 20 in the bright bulge direction to about 25 at the pole. band_for keeps one image per 50 pc cell of the observer's place (a move of 20 ly changes it by less than 0.02 mag), in memory or in .npy files (MemoryBandStore, FileBandStore), under a key that names the cell, the galaxy, the limit, the size and every constant the image depends on. [8.0.3213] - 2026-11-05

Headline: The update's cache warm-up gets four hours instead of thirty minutes, and a warm-up that is stopped says what stopped it instead of printing a traceback.

Changed

  • A longer limit (OPS.95). update.sh ran each warm stage under timeout 1800. A first warm-up after a new epoch on a real galaxy takes longer (it reached chunk 414 of 458 of the galaxy nodes in 30 minutes), so the run was ended with a KeyboardInterrupt traceback and nothing said why. The limit is now WARM_STAGE_SECONDS, default 14400 (4 hours), 0 for none, and the stage's first line says it: "Building the site's caches, stage 2 of 2, the full warm-up (time limit 4 hours, WARM_STAGE_SECONDS sets it; log: ...)". A value that is not a number is said and the default used.
  • One line instead of a traceback. When SIGTERM or a hangup ends planetgen warm, it prints one line saying what ended it and that a rerun continues, and exits 143 (SIGTERM), 129 (hangup) or 130 (Ctrl+C): "The cache warm-up was ended by update.sh's time limit for this stage (14400 s, WARM_STAGE_SECONDS). What it stored is kept: run planetgen warm --progress again and it continues where it stopped." The run is still marked cancelled in Redis, so its workers stop as before.
  • Cancellers leave a reason. The update guard's cancel and stop-all each leave one line for the process they are about to signal, in stop-reasons in the state folder (admin/stop_reason.py), and the run reads it, so the line names who stopped it. update.sh's limit is told to the run by environment and recognized when it has passed. A signal with no reason says so.
  • The final warning says what was kept. When a stage does not finish, update.sh's warning says whether it failed (with the status) or ran out of its limit, that what it stored is kept, and that planetgen warm --progress or the next ./update.sh continues.

[8.0.3205] - 2026-11-04

Headline: The first fill of a galaxy works out its bright-star band shares about fifteen times faster, with every star drawn as before.

Changed

  • PERF.232: the band shares of a first sector fill were most of its time, and most of that was work that could only come to 0. A sector fill asks, for every luminosity band from 100 Lsun up and every population, what share of the population's living stars the band holds (star_population._bright_fraction), which weighs about 8,000 masses of the IMF grid per threshold. For an old population nearly all of those stars are dead, or not yet off the main sequence, in the ages the population spans, and each was still worked out in full (the evolved-track corners, the thermal-pulse windows, the main-sequence crossing) to find it weighed nothing. Three changes, none of which moves a number:
    • A star whose bright windows all lie outside its population's age window now measures exactly 0 without them being worked out (star_population._outside_window: the windows lie between the main-sequence lifetime and the end of the last phase, and AgeLaw.weight is exactly 0 outside the window). A population's living count and the list of masses that can count at any threshold are worked out once for all thresholds (_fraction_terms) instead of once per threshold.
    • post_main_sequence.Timeline.bright_pieces, which finds the stretches of a track that clear a luminosity, runs its arithmetic in one numba pass over the samples (physics/bright_piece_kernel.py) instead of two dozen small array operations; a track with a sample that is not a number takes the array path as before.
    • An isochrone remembers the span and the lifetime of each mass it is asked about (datasets/isochrones._Isochrone._memo), and builds the sorted table its lifetime reads once, not on every call: a main-sequence crossing asks the same mass at a dozen ages. Measured on one 4-core machine, each from a cold folder: test_a_new_seed_replaces_the_old_only_before_any_sector took 1,478 s on main and about 430 s now, and the band shares inside it, sampled while it ran, took about 890 s before and about 60 s after. Every share of 98 asked (seven thresholds, every population, three mass ranges) is the same float as on main, and tests/test_bright_measure_exactness.py holds the three changes to the way they were worked out before, to the last bit. What is left of that test (the plan, the sampling tables, the sector's own systems) is not the shares. generation-output: unchanged

[8.0.3156] - 2026-11-04

Headline: Nebulae on the Galaxy Map are irregular, wispy shapes taken from the galaxy's gas and star-forming density, not circles.

Changed

  • MAP.365. A nebula is no longer a round sprite or a random blob per object. For each node the map draws, a new read-only endpoint (GET /galaxy/nebula-volume?key=<node key>, /api/galaxy/nebula-volume) samples the model's density (galaxy.nebula_density) at points on one absolute lattice (galaxy/nebula_volume.py): every lattice point in the node that a nebula reaching the node holds, with a strength from the density and the family of the nebula it is nearest to in its own radii. A nebula that crosses a node or sector border is drawn half by each node, with no seam, and the lattice gets finer (and the density adds noise octaves, so more filaments) as the nodes get finer. A dense core fades unevenly into a soft edge; a planetary nebula or a supernova remnant is a shell. Nothing is stored, so there is no migration and no epoch: the same galaxy draws the same shapes.
  • The map draws the points as soft splats (static/nebulavolume.js chooses and decodes, static/nebulavolumelayer.js draws). Where nebulae overlap on the screen their colors add up in a half-resolution target, and a full-screen pass bends the sum under a cap that keeps its hue, so a crowd of nebulae never washes to white. The group circles of MAP.176 and the per-nebula circle and GEN.75 mesh give way where a node's volume shows; the circles stay far out and while a volume loads, and a browser that cannot render to a float target keeps them. The family switches of the Menu switch the volumes too.
  • The tests hold a nebula's outline away from a circle (the circularity of its projected points, with the model's own clouds and a stand-in), two blocks that share a nebula drawing each place once, the same points whichever object it is, the node reader against a stored nebula, the capped sum against the shader's own output at every pixel of a browser frame, and the volume's packed bytes.

[8.0.3141] - 2026-11-04

Headline: a galaxy's first sector fill now keeps the bright-star tables in a folder, so it takes about 36 seconds and 0.5 GB instead of 267 seconds and 1.8 GB.

Changed

  • The bright-star sampling tables are kept on disk in production (PERF.188, PERF.218). A first sector fill built hundreds of tables, 717,000 distinct track evaluations, in every process that filled a sector. They are now kept as small files in /var/cache/planetgen/band-tables and read back by the next process that asks for the same table. The file name holds a key of every file of the planetgen package, of the downloaded datasets, of the Python and numpy versions and of every constant of tuning, so a changed generator file or a new download never reads an old table; a new key removes the folders of older versions of the code. A table read back is the table that was made (numbers are written as Python writes them), so the output and the golden digest are the same. A host without the folder builds the tables as before; PLANETGEN_BAND_TABLE_CACHE names another folder, or none when empty.
  • Setup makes the folder. examples/apache/create-cache-dir.sh, which install.sh and update.sh run, creates it owned by the web user whose workers write it (mode 750).

[8.0.3116] - 2026-11-04

Headline: A planet with no star can now be built through the one planet chain: it keeps the air its own gravity and heat allow, and it is warmed by its own heat instead of sitting at the 2.725 K floor.

Changed

  • The air of a body with no light (GEN.1111). The atmosphere table's shoreline rows (d1 to d5) measure a body against the starlight and the luminosity of its host; a body with no host has neither, so the star cannot strip its air and it sits far inside the shoreline (NO_LIGHT_DELTA, a sentinel, not a tuned value: any large negative number gives the same row). The star's wind pressure at a body with no star is zero, so it has no magnetopause to hold off a wind that is not there (magnetism.magnetopause_rp gives None).
  • A body with no star is warmed by its own heat. The temperature of a rocky planet whose host is starless, with or without air, adds the heat of its interior and its tide (internal_heat_flux_w_m2 and tidal_flux_w_m2) to the flux it radiates, as a giant's already did. Under a star that heat is below a part in a thousand of the absorbed flux for an ordinary rocky planet and is left out, so no lit planet changes. (A strongly tide-heated moon is the case where it is not that small; that is a separate question, not changed here.)

[8.0.3095] - 2026-11-01

Headline: A planet or moon's page now has a Day and night panel: a clock that counts its own day at the real rate, the state of its day and night in words, and the day and night hours of each latitude band beside the band's temperature.

Added

  • The day-and-night counter (UX.243). On the page of a planet or moon that has a stored state of day and night, a clock counts the object's own solar day at its real rate: the day number since 1 January 2000, 12:00 UTC (the same moment for every object, so two pages agree), the time into the day, and whether it is day or night with the time left of it. A tidally locked body has no clock; the panel says that one face stays toward its star (or its planet, for a moon), with a permanent day side and night side. A body that has no night says so. The page says that the picture of the body turns much faster than the real rotation, so the picture's speed and the clock stay apart. Beside the clock the seven latitude bands (or the seven rings of a locked world) are laid out with their annual mean temperature, their day and night hours and their state, each number with its unit. The values are the ones already stored (GEN.1097, GEN.1108), so there is no schema or API change; a body made before them has no panel.

Fixed

  • The browser test's bright-star rows. test_web_a11y.py wrote bright-star rows one column short of what the scatter writes now, so every page check failed building its database; the row has its last column again.

The scatter stored the first star and the fill rebuilt the second, so the check that the built star is the stored member failed and the system was left a single star. The record and the companion mass are floats now, so both sides make one star.

[8.0.3050] - 2026-11-01

Headline: The stars that share a system now have the masses real binaries have, with a surplus of near-equal twins in close pairs and lighter companions for massive stars.

Changed

  • A companion's mass is drawn from the measured mass-ratio law (GEN.951). It was the primary's mass times a ratio uniform from 0.1 to 1. Moe and Di Stefano (2017, Table 13) find the ratio follows a power law that depends on how massive the primary is and how wide the pair is, with an excess of twins (ratio above 0.95) at short periods. A Sun-like primary keeps a near-flat ratio and gets 12% twins (it was 6%); a massive star's companions lean to light stars (the mean ratio is 0.38 for a 12 solar mass primary, it was 0.55) and have few twins. The period is still drawn after the masses, so the ratio is the average over the four periods the paper tabulates, each in the share of the star's companions that sit there.
  • The stars of the systems still follow the single-star mass function. The primary mass function is derived from the same law, so the share of primaries and companions at each mass is consistent with it: systems per star born moved from 0.697 to 0.695, and systems per solar mass from 1.128 to 1.124. Past the top cell of the mass grid the primary function continues the line of its last two cells, where it was held flat.
  • The mean mass of a pair is worked out from the same law. The widest wide-pair axis a place keeps (and the odds of a close or wide companion) use the mean ratio of the primary's companions instead of 0.55.

TODO items resolved: GEN.951.

[8.0.3049] - 2026-11-01

Headline: A belt the giant branch reached keeps the part outside the envelope, and a white dwarf's belt records what its star did to it and how much rock the mass loss threw inward.

Changed

  • GEN.1072: StarSystem._apply_star_history used to drop a belt whose inner edge lay inside the progenitor's engulfment radius whole. The belt now goes through remnant_orbits.engulf_belt first: the part inside the radius is lost and the part outside keeps its share of the mass (physics/belt_history.engulf, the power-law surface density), so a belt that reaches past the envelope survives as its outer part; one wholly inside is still removed. remnant_orbits.widen_for_mass_loss widens a belt's edges as before and then runs belt_history.mass_loss: with a giant left in the system a share of the belt (half the fraction of the star's mass that was lost) is thrown inward and its mass falls by that much. The belt keeps its history sentences (history), the mass it formed with (formed_mass_kg) and the mass thrown inward (scattered_mass_kg); remnant_orbits.pollution_rate_g_s(bodies) turns that mass into the accretion rate on the white dwarf. The history and the scattered mass are worked out at build and are not stored. The belt_history module, rows BHS1 to BHS5 and CP2 leave the wiring register (read now). The independent white dwarf pollution draw is unchanged. Changes the belts of white dwarfs and of any star with a swallowing radius.

[8.0.3048] - 2026-11-01

Headline: A system now has a clearance ledger that says where a planet, moon or belt may sit, ready for the generator to draw from.

For a star or a close pair taken as one body it holds the spans of distance where a new planet of a given mass and eccentricity may sit: the host's window (the engulfment floor, the Holman and Wiegert limits at every level above it), less the stretch round each planet where two planets would stand closer than ten mutual Hill radii (on both sides, and across a belt), less each belt with the planet's five Hill radii. Nothing in the generator reads it yet, so no system changes; the wiring that replaces _orbit_floor_au, the per-star stability reads and the spacing pass, and fixes the pair of planets 9.93 mutual Hill radii apart in triple seed 208 (GEN.1023), rides merge train 10.

[8.0.3025] - 2026-10-31

Headline: The galaxy's cluster field is now built ahead by the warm-up, in small saved parts, and the web only reads it.

Changed

  • The galaxy's cluster field (its globular clusters, satellites and young open clusters as one field the density model reads) took 20 to 60 seconds to build in whatever process first needed it, nearly all of it working out the mean system mass of each distinct age. It is now the first family of the warm-up's opening phase (warm-cluster-field, galaxy/field_job.py): one queued unit for every 1,000 ages works out its part and writes it as a file in the state folder, so every unit is a fraction of a second to a few seconds however busy the machine is; when the last part is in, the field is made from the rows and the parts and written as galaxy-field/<signature>.field by a rename. A warm-up that stopped carries on from the parts that are there. The signature names the stored rows and the source of the code that decides the numbers, so a changed row or formula is a new file, and the file is read through an unpickler that allows only the field's own classes.

A visitor's request for a galaxy of more than 1,500 components that has no file is refused at once with the 503 and Retry-After of the cache guard (cause missing) instead of building for a minute against the daemon's request limit; a worker, a command or the warm-up still builds it in its own process when no file is there, and a small galaxy is still built in the request (about a second).
  • ComponentField takes the mean system masses by age as an optional argument, so the parts can hand them in; the numbers it gives are the same as before.

Fixed

  • A page that needed the cluster field after every generation run no longer waits a minute for it inside a web request.

Headline: The pages that will explain where the numbers come from have one address scheme, one link helper, and a word check that keeps the doubt words out of the rest of the site.

Added

  • web/lib/reference_urls.py: the addresses of the References pages (DOC.87, References R1). reference_path(kind, id) gives the address of an entry: /references, /references/papers#paper-<doi>, /references/data, /references/method/<area>#<value>, /references/stand-ins/<id>, /references/fitted, /references/speculative#class-<id>, /references/gaps, /references/scorecard and /references/about. The words that tell a reader the site is a model (speculative, stand-in, tweak, fitted, tuned, educated guess, tier, generator, generated, seed, simulated, model, version, and their forms) belong only on the References pages and the admin pages. "Level" is not on the list; "sea level" is in universe.
  • tests/test_references_crawl.py: the page crawl. It renders the Help pages and the class pages, reads the Document of ten seeded systems, every sheet label and every sheet source line, and fails on an out-of-universe word that its KNOWN list does not name. [8.0.2999] - 2026-10-31

Headline: A rocky planet's magnetic field now comes from its core cooling on its own curve, not from a lifetime drawn at random.

Changed

  • The core has its own temperature (GEN.838). The interior heat model kept one temperature for the mantle and the core, so the heat crossing the core-mantle boundary, the inner core and the dynamo had no curve of their own. A second state, the core's temperature, now cools beside the mantle's (physics/core_heat.py): the heat crosses a boundary layer set by the mantle's viscosity, the core freezes an inner core as it cools (its latent heat slows the cooling), and the dynamo runs while that heat and the inner core's growth leave power over the heat the core conducts down its own adiabat. The Earth ends at 4,080 K with an inner core of 0.4 of its radius and 5.7 TW across the boundary. A body's stored heat flow and Urey ratio are unchanged, and a body with no metal has no core.
  • The magnetic field reads the core. A rocky planet's dipole moment is the Earth's times the buoyancy-flux scaling of its core (radius squared, power to the 1/3, density to the 1/6); a dead core has none (Mars), a heavier planet's core stays liquid and keeps a dynamo (2 to 10 Earth masses). The dynamo lifetime draw and the stagnant-lid factor are gone: the lid acts through the mantle's temperature. Mercury keeps its observed 3e19 A m2. Stand-ins CC1 to CC11 are in the gap plan registry (section 6.19).
  • Generator epoch bump (numbered at merge): the stored magnetic moment, dipole class and magnetopause of rocky planets change, and so do the radiation doses and habitability scores that follow them. generation-output: changed

The ring now draws its clusters under eps Gamma M_T (Reina-Campos and Kruijssen 2017): the Toomre mass of its gas surface density and rotation, a tenth of it into stars and the ring's bound share of those into one cluster. For the Milky Way shape that is 1.6e4 solar masses, never over 1e5. The new module is physics/cluster_maximum_mass.py.
  • Passing clouds disrupt the ring's clusters. Gieles et al. 2006 as Kruijssen et al. 2014 put it in the ring: a cluster of 1e4 solar masses and half-mass radius 0.5 pc lasts 5.7 Myr. Over 40 seeds the ring now holds 0.6 young clusters above 5e3 solar masses on average (none old above 5e4) against 4.2 and 11 before. The stored clusters of every barred galaxy change, so it needs an epoch.
  • The ring's gas surface density is a registered stand-in (the inflow times a 50 Myr residence over the ring's area, about 800 solar masses per pc2), rows CMX1 to CMX7 in the stand-in list. The disc's flat 1e6 cap stays until GEN.1196.
