[8.0.2532] - 2026-10-29

Headline: A generation run that stopped partway can be finished instead of wiped: planetgen finish-run, or "Finish the last run" on the Generate page.

Added

  • Finish the last run. A run that was killed, ran out of database memory or was cancelled carries on from the first stage that did not finish, on the same galaxy: the stages it finished are kept, the stage that stopped runs again from its start (a sector stage skips the sectors it already saved, a scatter empties what it rewrites first), and every stage after it runs as it would have. The galaxy ends the same as an uninterrupted run (same seed, same sectors, same scatter).
  • Where. planetgen finish-run [--run ID], the "Finish the last run" card on the Generate page (it also goes on with the steps of that job that never started, for example the link and the sector paths of a New galaxy), and the typed command finish run. A failed run now prints the planetgen finish-run line.
  • Safe. A run records the galaxy's seed and the PlanetGen build it worked on, and is carried on only while both are still the ones it started on, in the database it worked on. A run is carried on once; a finish that stops is finished in turn.

Changed

  • The run record keeps what each stage finished, and the starting run's galaxy seed, build and the run it carried on. The Queue page's Retry is unchanged.

Fixed

The distance from the centre was found by squaring the three coordinates, which overflows a float for a coordinate that large; it uses the overflow-safe hypotenuse now, and a point that far gets the normal empty answer. Regression tests cover three far points (TEST.451).
  • test_galaxy_gen.py took half an hour and stopped single tests at the 900 s limit. Its sparse-wedge test generated a dense sector with every system's planets, moons and solved air (the "settle-job timeout" Core 5 saw). These tests are about which sectors a run makes and where, so the whole file now makes planetless systems; it runs in 18 minutes and its slowest test takes 7 (TEST.451).

Headline: The hot-zone Yellow share that fell to 0 since the solved air is explained, and the class census now expects it.

Fixed

  • GEN.896 is not a generator fault, so the census ranges move instead of the generator. Bisecting the hot-zone draws (G2V, M2V, K5V, F5V) found that before the solved air (epoch 106) 29 of 69 hot-zone G2V planets held 1 to 26 kPa of air whatever their mass (Mercury-sized rocks of 0.003 to 0.15 Earth masses at 450 to 600 K), and that air shielded the ground from the ultraviolet and the dose: Radiation scored Yellow on those, so the overall colour could. Now the same tiny hot rocks keep no air (1 of 70), the unshielded ultraviolet index is 1,000 to 26,000 (Red from 300) or the dose is over 1 Sv a year, Radiation is Red and caps the overall colour at Red. K5V hot planets, whose light is dim in the ultraviolet, still score Yellow at the old rate (24 percent). The eight hot-zone Yellow ranges (A0V, F5V, G2V, M2V, planets and moons) now read 0 to 4 percent with the reason in their source, and the known-anomaly entry for GEN.896 is gone (GEN.896).

[8.0.2527] - 2026-10-29

Headline: planetgen galaxy is one run in the queue, so one estimate covers the whole galaxy.

Changed

The estimate shows the whole list, the Queue page shows one run, and the same seed makes the same galaxy at one worker and at four. The process that starts the run only follows it; the work between a stage's units moved into the stage's command.
  • A stage that cannot start, or cannot end, fails the run and says which. The empty-the-table step before a scatter and the store-the-record step after it used to run in the starting process; they now run in a worker, and a failure shows as "stage X could not start" or "the end of stage X failed" instead of a unit that looked done.
  • A link that fails now fails the run (it only warned before), and a failed galaxy prints the planetgen link --since line to run it again.
  • A stage with nothing to do is stored as skipped (no sector saved since the run started, nothing to backfill), so it adds nothing to the estimates.

Headline: Epoch and migration numbers are renumbered by one script when a branch has to follow main, instead of by hand.

Changed

Run on a tree that holds the branch's changes (merged or rebased onto main, even with epochs.json in conflict), it renames the branch's migrations to follow main's newest and rewrites their revision ids, appends the branch's epochs to main's epochs.json with the next numbers, makes the schema_v<head>.sql.gz fixture the first migration is tested from out of main's schema.sql and moves its README line, and changes v<old>, <old> and epoch <old> in the lines the branch added. --check reports whether the numbers already follow main's and --dry-run shows the changes; it refuses when two own migrations share a number or main already holds the fixture. A test builds a main and a branch in a throwaway git repository and covers both the renumbering and the conflicted epochs.json (OPS.71).

Added

  • The change plan engine, as a library (ADM.58). planetgen/admin/plans.py holds a plan: an ordered list of operations (move an orbit or a system, set an aspect, regenerate with a keep set, add, remove) on stored systems. It works the whole effect out on copies without writing anything: every field that would change, with its before and after, the neighbours the spacing pass has to move (listed as indirect), a sentence per operation and the layout problems the plan leaves. Each plan has a state (draft, requested, proposed, approved, applied, undone, stale, rejected, withdrawn), and every move records who made it and in which role. A proposed plan is stale when an object it touches was edited after it was proposed, but not when the nightly orbital update moved it; a move then shows its drift and can be planned again from the new values. Operations and the systems as they will be use the same envelope as the remote upload. No page, route, table or stored value changes; the store (ADM.59) and the apply job (ADM.60) come next.

Headline: A planet or moon whose surface is hotter than its mantle's melting point no longer crashes or hangs the generator.

Fixed

  • A surface above the mantle's liquidus broke the interior heat model (GEN.856). A mobile-lid body there divided by a zero temperature drop (or took a complex power), and a stagnant-lid one ended with a mantle cooler than its own surface. Such a body is now a magma ocean: its mantle sits at the surface's temperature, the melt carries out what the body makes (the decay heat of its silicate, and a tide that flexes a molten body), and the heat released over its age is what it made. A mobile lid with no temperature drop carries no heat. Bodies under a cooler surface are unchanged.

[8.0.2508] - 2026-10-29

Headline: Worlds with oxygenic life now grow the oxygen that life makes, and every world's life reaches each stage on a timeline drawn from its own temperature and air, so animals and civilizations appear again where the air allows them.

Changed

  • Biogenic oxygen (GEN.855). A world whose life splits water (Chlorophyll a, Blue-Optimized Porphyrins) and has a sunlit sea (a surface or hycean ocean) now holds the oxygen its life has had time to make: the balance of organic carbon burial, volcanic reductants and rock weathering, after the first oxygen has used up the reductants of the ocean, crust and air (the reduced gases of the air burn away). Earth's numbers reproduce its 22.7 kPa and a delay of 0.7 Gyr after the first photosynthesis; another light, sea, heat or mantle gives another oxygen. The greenhouse, surface temperature, ozone, radiation doses, atmosphere colour and habitability score are made again from the new air. Retinal, anoxygenic and radiotrophic life make no oxygen.
  • A life timeline from physics (GEN.750). The three fixed paces are gone. Each world draws five hard-step waits (abiogenesis, photosynthesis, complex cells, multicellularity, civilization), quickened by the Boltzmann factor of its surface temperature, with the first light harvesting earlier for simpler chemistries and the wait for complex cells starting only once the air holds oxygen. A forced technological civilization is a timeline conditioned on finishing inside the world's age. The step means are Boss's choice (0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3 and 60 Gyr): for oxygenic life at the reference temperature about 41 in 100 worlds reach animals and 2 in 100 a civilization.
  • Oxygenic chemistries no longer need oxygen already in the air; they need a sunlit sea. Migration 0156 no longer reads the removed schedule function; it uses the table directly. generation-output: changed

TODO items resolved: GEN.855, GEN.750. Added: stand-in registry rows LF49 to LF56 (section 6.18) and BO1 to BO9 (section 6.21 of the gap-filling plan).

[8.0.2458] - 2026-10-29

Headline: A world with water vapour in its air is no longer too hot: the vapour thins with height, as it does on the Earth, and the greenhouse sums over that profile.

Changed

  • The water vapour of the greenhouse thins with height (GEN.812). physics/infrared_opacity.py took the surface's vapour pressure as the mixing ratio all the way up, so an Earth twin whose air held 0.77 of saturation at its own temperature came out at 319 K, not 288 K. It now thins the vapour with height (the humidity falls linearly with pressure, Manabe and Wetherald 1967; the temperature follows the troposphere), sums the water continuum over the layers and counts the H2O bands and far wing for the pressure each layer sits at. The Earth twin lands at 288 K, and the surface temperature of every body with water vapour in its air changes.
  • A grey cloud depth for the longwave effect of clouds (GEN.812). The module is a clear-sky greenhouse, but a body's albedo is its all-sky one, so one grey depth (0.35 at the Earth's surface humidity, scaled with the humidity, nil without liquid water) stands for the cloud. It is a stand-in with registry rows GH1 to GH4 in docs/design/research/stand-in-values.md.
  • heat_capacity_ratio moved from atmosphere_state to mixture, where the vapour profile and the closure both read it.

Headline: A rocky world's mantle is no hotter than the melting curve of its own rock allows, and a body measures its interior heat against its own surface temperature.

Changed

  • The mantle's ceiling is a liquidus, not a fixed 3,500 K (GEN.735). A young mantle starts at the temperature its assembly heat gives and is held at the liquidus at the middle of the mantle (a_l (p + p_l)^c_l with Manske et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.18718 Table 1: 310.317, 29.102 GPa, 0.5337). That is about 3,100 K for the Earth and 1,900 K for a Moon-sized body, where every body had 3,500 K. A stiff mantle now leaves its ceiling sooner, so an Earth twin at 0.1 Gy gives 3 to 30 times the heat of 4.5 Gy (4 to 33 before).
  • The body's own surface temperature (GEN.735). The birth temperature and a mobile lid's drop use the surface temperature of the body once its climate is known, not a fixed 273 K. A mantle too cold to convect (Ea / R T over 600) loses no heat and warms with its own radiogenic heat until it does; a cold small body far from its star starts there.
  • Not built: the separate core temperature (Thiriet et al. 2019 was not readable). Generator epoch bump (numbered at merge): every rocky body's mantle temperature, heat flux and Urey ratio can change.

[8.0.2436] - 2026-10-28

Headline: A greenhouse model on real line data is built (not yet used by the generator): doubling carbon dioxide warms Earth by about a kelvin with its vapour held, and Titan's haze brings it to its measured surface.

Added

  • Downloaded infrared line data (GEN.715). update.sh now also fetches the ExoMol correlated-k tables of water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane (about 1.3 GB) and the HITRAN collision-induced absorption of 11 gas pairs (about 0.2 GB), reduces them to 6.5 MB of band tables in the data cache and deletes the downloads. Generation requires them like the other datasets; --disregard-missing-data takes the labelled stand-ins instead.
  • A one-dimensional radiative-convective model (GEN.715, GEN.717, GEN.718). physics/radiative_convective.py (the line opacity is physics/line_opacity.py) finds the surface temperature at which an air's adiabat, topped by a radiative stratosphere, sends the absorbed sunlight back to space, band by band and g point by g point, with Manabe and Wetherald's humidity, a water continuum, collision-induced pairs, and an optional share of the sunlight that a haze takes high up.

Changed

  • The model is built but not wired. radiative_convective.warming returns the surface temperature, the greenhouse factor G, the tropopause and the whole profile; atmosphere_state.greenhouse_warming keeps the grey closure of GEN.703 that the surface-air iteration calls several times per planet, because the new model takes one to several seconds a call. Checked, not tuned: a doubling of carbon dioxide with the vapour held warms 1.0 K (GEN.717), Titan with 60 percent of its sunlight absorbed in its haze sits at 93 K against the measured 94 K (GEN.718), clear-sky Earth at 276 K, Mars at 215 K, Venus at 711 K. Nothing the generator stores changes.

Fixed

  • The moist adiabat took the wrong slope across the saturation corner. A step that started unsaturated and crossed into saturation used the saturated slope for its whole length, so the top of the column came out up to 10 K too warm just below the corner and then fell as the surface warmed.

The rest are sealed or carbon-rich worlds whose greenhouse takes them past the critical point of water; their steam envelope is the planet's own water and test_planets now bounds the air by it and not by a flat pressure.

[8.0.2412] - 2026-10-28

Headline: A table whose clustered index has a page the server cannot read can now be rebuilt in two steps with planetgen repair-db --salvage and --reload, and the rows the page took come back from the parity file.

Changed

  • planetgen repair-db --salvage TABLE and --reload TABLE (DB.48). With the server started with innodb_force_recovery = 1 and the website and generation stopped, --salvage dumps every readable row of the table to a file (exactly, nothing rounded), then drops the table and makes it again empty. After a normal restart --reload inserts the rows back with their ids, checks the count, and runs the sector repair, which rebuilds the sectors that lost rows from the parity file. It refuses, changing nothing, when the table cannot be read and the server is not in force recovery, when a dump is already waiting, or when a normal server counts other rows than were dumped. An interrupted reload is finished by running it again. --restore-sectors (with --reload sectors) also puts back sector rows the parity file holds and the table lacks. repair-db now names the unreadable tables when it lists unreadable sectors. Only the tables a sector's checksum covers can be rebuilt this way.
  • repair-db can rebuild a sector whose own sectors row is gone (it puts the row back first).

[8.0.2410] - 2026-10-28

Headline: planetgen repair-db rebuilds damaged sectors from the parity file, so a flipped value or a lost row in a sector can be mended instead of regenerating the sector.

Changed

  • planetgen repair-db [--shell N] [--sector SHELL BAND WEDGE] [--dry-run] (DB.47). Finds the sectors whose rows no longer hash to the checksum sealed for them and rebuilds them from their group in the parity file (up to two damaged sectors of a group at once with the default settings). The rebuilt block must hash to the stored checksum before anything is written, the rows are updated, inserted or deleted in one transaction, and the sector is checked again before the commit. The columns the orbit update rewrites are left alone on every row that still exists. A sector the parity cannot mend (a record behind the database as well, a sector in no group, more damage than parity blocks) is listed with the reason and left as it is, and the command exits 1; a table the server cannot read is DB.48's case. A parity file that is itself damaged is made again from the database. --dry-run writes nothing.
  • A sealed sector that no longer hashes to its checksum is never taken into the parity file (protect_sector, so refresh-parity and the save hook leave it for repair-db): the sweep would otherwise have recorded the damage as the truth.

[8.0.2407] - 2026-10-28

Headline: An optional parity file beside the database can now rebuild a damaged sector: it is kept current as sectors are saved, edited and deleted, and planetgen refresh-parity builds it for a galaxy made before.

Changed

  • The parity file (DB.46). With the new setting parity.enabled on (off by default; parity.dir, parity.group_size 32 and parity.parity_blocks 2 are the others), a log of Reed-Solomon parity records is kept outside the database for groups of up to 32 sectors of about the same size that sit far apart in sector id, so that two damaged sectors of a group can be rebuilt from the rest (the rebuild is DB.47) at about 7 percent of the sectors' size in disk space. Every save, edit and deletion commits first and then updates the parity (Connection.after_commit); a sector whose parity is behind is reported as unprotected by check-db, never as damaged, and a record behind the database is made again, not treated as damage. A sector whose group has a damaged member is left alone.
  • planetgen refresh-parity [--compact] [--limit N] makes the file current for the whole database (marked and never-sealed sectors, sealed sectors the file lacks, members whose sector is gone) and --compact drops the dead space an append-only log leaves.
  • sector_export writes a sector as bytes (every covered row, ids included, in the checksum's own encoding) and reads them back, so a rebuilt block can be turned into rows with their ids; storage_checksum.checksum_of takes rows from either.
  • The design note (docs/design/operations/db-check-and-parity-repair.md, 5.10) records what was built and where it differs from the sketch.

[8.0.2393] - 2026-10-28

Headline: planetgen bring-to-epoch brings a stored galaxy to the running generator epoch without a full regeneration: it generates again only the sectors an epoch change altered and leaves edited sectors alone.

Changed

  • planetgen bring-to-epoch [--dry-run] (GEN.764, step 3). Reads the epoch each stage of the stored galaxy was made under and the stages the epochs since changed (affects). It generates again, in address order, every galaxy-placed sector whose fill is behind (the sector is deleted and made again from its address and the galaxy's seed, then the paths around it are settled), makes the species of an older population epoch again (a species edited by hand is kept) and runs the population pass. It says each sector and species step; --dry-run lists them and changes nothing; a sector that fails is reported and the others go on; running it again resumes an interrupted run, since each sector records its epoch when it is saved.
  • Edited sectors are skipped and listed. The admin audit log is the record of edits (a sector, system, star, planet, moon, belt, comet, facility or phenomenon edit in it): the sector is left alone with the actions named. An edit of an object since deleted cannot be traced to its sector, and a sector edited before the audit log existed looks unedited.
  • Refusals say why. A plan made under an epoch that changed the galaxy's shape needs a full regeneration (the epochs are named); a scatter made under an older epoch has to be drawn again first (planetgen clear-scatter, then planetgen scatter), because the sectors are filled from it. Neither changes anything.
  • util.generator_epoch.epochs_changing(stage, recorded) names the epochs after a recorded one that altered a stage; galaxy.epoch_record.needs is its public stale test. The page button and the queue run are the next step.

Every writer that changes a covered column (generation, renames, edits, facilities, regenerating a system, deleting a system, the nebula clean-up, the sector page's edits) marks the sector's parity_dirty flag in its own transaction without moving its change time, and a test lists every such writer so a new one cannot be added unmarked. planetgen check-db storage (also in the default list) reports a sector whose flag is clear but whose rows no longer match its checksum as damage, and the sectors with no current checksum as one warning. Nothing seals a sector yet: that comes with the parity update (DB.46/48), so today every sector is reported as not yet protected.

Headline: A magnetised world now has radiation belts, with a dose for any orbit inside them.

Added

A body with air starts its belts above the air. The dose rate behind 100 mil of aluminium at any orbit follows from Earth's belts scaled by the field, and is checked against Earth (LEO, navigation orbit, geostationary, the slot between the belts) and Jupiter (the doses at Io, Europa and Ganymede, and the belts ending inside Callisto's orbit). Nothing is stored or drawn, so generated worlds are unchanged.

[8.0.2380] - 2026-10-28

Headline: The tide of a body's real orbit heats it and wears down its spin: Io-like moons melt and radiate, Mercury-like worlds are caught in a resonance, hot Jupiters lock, and the Moon-like ones stay cold.

Changed

  • Tidal heating comes from the orbit's real eccentricity (GEN.737). A rocky or icy planet or moon is heated by the eccentricity tide of the orbit stored with it (Peale, Cassen and Reynolds 1979), from the eccentricity of GEN.727. The drawn forced eccentricity and the random 1 to 50 times resonance boost of small icy moons are gone, and so is the tide of an icy moon only: planets and rocky bodies have one too.
  • A rocky body's rheology has two states. Solid, its Love number comes from its rigidity (the Moon's 0.021) and Q is 100, which gives the Moon 2e8 W. If that heat is at least the body's own and would melt its mantle, the melt erupts and carries the heat out, the mantle holds the melt temperature and the partly molten body is flexed far more: Io comes out at 9e13 W, 2.2 W/m2.
  • The heat is stored and counted. The tide goes into the interior heat model (a heat source of the mantle, and the melt state), is stored in tidal_flux_w_m2 for every rocky and icy planet and moon, and is added to the body's own heat flow in the habitability energy term and the ice-shell thickness. The own heat flow (internal_heat_flux_w_m2) and the Urey ratio leave the tide out.
  • Enceladus makes the tide alone. Its equilibrium tide is about 0.4 GW; the 16 GW it radiates is an open problem in the literature that the old boost hid.
  • A planet's day is its birth spin worn down by tides (GEN.731). A rocky planet is born spinning at the rate and tilt the giant impacts that built it leave (Kokubo and Genda 2010: Gaussian components, a median day of 2 to 3 hours, an isotropic axis), a moon or a giant from its own range, and the tide of what it orbits then slows the spin for the age of the star, with the body's own Love number and quality factor (the same that circularise its orbit). A close body ends locked, one turn per orbit with its axis upright; an eccentric one is caught in a spin-orbit resonance (Mercury's 3:2 at its eccentricity of 0.2; windows from Makarov 2012); a far one keeps its spin. A hot Jupiter locks in about a hundred thousand years; the Moon, in tens of millions. This replaces the flat 8 to 48 hour day of rocky planets, so typical planetary days are now much shorter than the Solar System's (24 hours): the source simulates the last giant impacts only.
  • Stand-ins recorded. Rows TH1 to TH10 and SP1 to SP10 in the stand-in registry (GEN.725). generation-output: changed

[8.0.2379] - 2026-10-28

Headline: Planets and moons now travel on real ellipses, with seasons from the changing distance to their star.

Changed

  • Planets and moons have an eccentricity and a mutual inclination (GEN.727). A planet's eccentricity is drawn from the Kepler laws (Van Eylen et al. 2019: a half-Gaussian of width 0.083 for a system of several planets, a mixture peaking near 0.26 for a lone one), a regular moon's forced eccentricity from 0.001 to 0.01 (kept for good, as Io's is by its neighbours) and a captured moon's from the thermal law, all cut where the orbit would leave the stable region (periapsis outside the Roche limit, apoapsis inside the Hill sphere). Tidal circularisation over the star's age pulls close planets and captured moons back toward a circle. Inclination is Rayleigh about a plane shared with the others (mutual inclination 1.6 degrees over the square root of two).
  • The state vector is the ellipse. Position and velocity come from the orbital elements, the stored distance is the semi-major axis, and the orbit update steps the state on its conic. The new eccentricity column (planets and moons, migration 0156) is stored; older rows read as a circle.
  • Light follows the orbit. A body's mean flux is the circular value over the square root of one minus e squared, its temperature range gains the swing between periapsis and apoapsis, and a lone star's flux_variation is that swing.
  • Spacing, belts, moon stability and the system map use periapsis and apoapsis. Orbit reach, the gap past a belt and between planets, and the moon stability check use the ellipse; the system map draws an ellipse for each orbit and the object page has an Eccentricity row.
  • Stand-ins recorded. The drawn laws and their source tiers and tweak levels are rows OE1 to OE11 in the stand-in registry (GEN.725). generation-output: changed

The second runs only with PLANETGEN_VERSION_GATE=1, which scripts/test.py full and full --check (the end-of-version run) set, as the budget test runs only when asked; it is skipped with that reason in a merge gate and while the golden files are written. Golden files are byte-identical for the same seed. A determinism break between one worker and four is therefore caught at the version gate and not at each generation merge. [8.0.2339] - 2026-10-25

Headline: What a small or hot planet loses from its air now comes from a model of its thermosphere and its star's XUV history, instead of a fixed ratio of temperatures and a rule of thumb.

Changed

  • Escape model (GEN.738). The exobase temperature is the mesopause plus a rise that goes with the star's XUV and is cooled by the carbon dioxide of the air, fitted to the upper-atmosphere model of Johnstone et al. 2018. Each species leaves by the Jeans flux through the exobase, at most what the air below can carry up, and the star's XUV decay over the body's age is integrated against the air that is left. The Earth keeps its nitrogen, oxygen, argon and carbon dioxide and loses its hydrogen and helium; Venus keeps all of its air; Mars keeps CO2 and nitrogen; Titan's hydrogen flux is within 15 percent of the measured 9.2e27 per second. The old exobase ratios, XUV exponent and logistic width (registry rows AM19 to AM21) are gone, and the two remaining cutoffs are labelled as numerical.
  • Envelope mass loss. The analytic fit of Kubyshkina et al. 2018 for a hydrogen envelope is in thermosphere.py and reproduces the nine planets of its Table 2 to a factor of 2.3 or better; it is not wired into the sub-Neptune rows yet. Nothing in the generator draws the mixture yet (it waits on GEN.411 and GEN.422), so no stored value changes today.
  • Tests for the Earth, Venus, Mars, Titan and the nine planets, fifteen stand-in registry rows (GEN.725, AM63 to AM77), a design note (atmospheric-escape-model.md) and the licences of the three papers read.

  • A worker killed (or lost to the out-of-memory killer) within 90 seconds of being started was not replaced for the rest of that time (TEST.371). The count of workers "started and not yet registered" (planetgen:workers:starting:<queue>, PERF.181) was only ever cleared by its 90 second expiry, so a worker that had registered was counted twice, once among the live ones and once among the starting ones, and the room left for a replacement stayed taken. A job then waited in the queue with no worker until the count ran out. A worker now takes itself off that count when it registers (workers.registered, called from the worker's register_birth). test_workers.py::test_a_worker_that_is_killed_is_replaced_and_the_queued_job_runs waited 90 s for this and passed or failed by a second (it failed alone 1 time in 3); it now takes under 5 s, and a new test holds the count.
  • test_cache_warmup.py::test_a_family_command_runs_alone_and_warms_only_its_family (TEST.377) expected run-population to refuse to be cut into units, but every registered command has an expansion now. It makes an inline command of its own to show the refusal. TODO items resolved: TEST.371, TEST.377 (TODO closes them after reading this). Added: none.

[8.0.2336] - 2026-10-25

Headline: A planet with an ocean and no land now has a carbon sink in the model, so its carbon dioxide no longer has to stay in the air.

Added

  • The carbon of a water world, as a module (GEN.814). An ocean deep enough to seal the seafloor (1 to 3 GPa) holds its carbon by ocean chemistry and the cations the early ocean leached from the crust; an unsealed world with no land loses carbon to the seafloor, as Kite and Ford 2018 and Krissansen-Totton and Catling 2017 describe. The generator does not call it yet; it joins the air solve with the surface-air work.

[8.0.2335] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The Galaxy Map has no sector boxes any more: a click selects the star or object under it and shows its details, and a double click flies to it.

Changed

  • No sector boxes on the Galaxy Map (MAP.297). Hovering or clicking the map no longer names, outlines, shades or opens a block of sectors; the blocks remain only as the data the map draws from, as the optional Cell grid, on a sector page's own map, and while a NAV end is chosen. The arrow keys no longer move among blocks.
  • A star takes the click (MAP.304). Every drawn star is picked from any distance (the nearest to the pointer, the brightest of those level with it): one click selects it and shows its details in the map's window, a click on nothing puts them away, a double click (or Enter on the selected one) flies the camera to it, a sector and a half away at the nearest. The wheel still zooms where it did. The map's help and hint text say so.

[8.0.2334] - 2026-10-25

Headline: A moon's makeup now follows from how it formed, so icy captured moons and rocky impact moons differ in density, ice and metal.

Changed

  • A moon's metal, rock, water and ice shares come from its origin (GEN.466). A disk moon of a giant planet gains ice past its disk's ice line (the disks of one giant's moons share a lifetime and an ice line) and turns from dry to carbonaceous rock with distance, an impact moon of a rocky planet is nearly dry and takes a few percent metal, and a captured moon is a Kuiper-belt-like mix of rock and ice with some ice lost. The water share is no longer drawn from the moon's class range.
  • A small moon's density comes from the tapered brittle compaction law (GEN.466, GEN.442). A moon lighter than 1e21 kg has voids that close with size and so a density that rises with its radius; a heavier one is solved from its composition with no macroporosity.

Changed

  • Delivered-water rows b1 to b4 (GEN.802). [8.0.2331] - 2026-10-25

Headline: Suggested facility ratings now read the host's Suitability, food rung, radiation domain and Flora and Fauna, so a facility on a hard-to-live-on world no longer rates Health and Housing from the overall score alone.

Changed

Health is now 0.4 Medical, 0.2 habitability, 0.2 radiation domain and 0.2 food rung (it was 0.5 and 0.5); Housing is 0.25 habitability, 0.25 Suitability, 0.3 Materials and 0.2 kind size (it was 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2); Resources on a living world takes 0.2 from its Flora and Fauna (biota) out of richness, Energy and nearness. [8.0.2330] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The browser tests no longer fail with "50 per 1 hour" rate-limit errors, and each app now follows its own API request limit.

Fixed

  • The API's default request limit (200 per day, 50 per hour per address) was taken from the first app made in a process and kept for every app made after it (Limiter.init_app keeps only the first default of a shared limiter). A test run builds many apps in one process, so a browser fixture that called the API from one address (sample_params makes about 7 calls per module) could not be given a different limit and ran into the hourly 50, which errored 259 browser tests at setup. The limit is now read from the current app's RATELIMIT_DEFAULT on each request. On a real server, which makes one app, nothing changes: the limit is still 200 per day and 50 per hour, and an empty setting still turns it off.
  • The browser test sites (habitability_site, map_site_support, test_web_a11y, test_web_browser_tables, test_web_settings_browser) now set RATELIMIT_DEFAULT = API_LIMIT_OFF, so their fixtures cannot be throttled. A route's own limits (login, writes) still apply to them.

Added

  • planetgen.api.limiter.API_LIMIT_OFF, the RATELIMIT_DEFAULT that turns the default limit off for a test harness.
  • Tests in test_web_security_limits.py that a direct API call is still limited by the default (429 with rate limit exceeded, per address), that API_LIMIT_OFF is never limited, that two apps in one process keep their own default in either order, and that the production default is unchanged. TODO items resolved: TEST.385 (TODO closes it after reading this). Added: none.

The Generate job's whole-job bar reads "roughly A to B left (not timed yet)", the Queue page's time left reads "A to B (not timed yet)", the Galaxy banner says "(nothing has been timed yet)", the deep database check's estimate says "not timed yet", and the estimate's source in the run record API is now "not timed yet" instead of "rough guess".

[8.0.2328] - 2026-10-25

Headline: An admin edit now works the light a planet sums over the stars out again before the scores are rewritten, so a body in a binary system no longer keeps a habitability score from before the edit.

Fixed

  • An edit leaves current scores (ADM.132). An admin edit (regenerate, class change, star change) already rewrote the habitability, Suitability and life scores of the edited body and its moons, and save_system_edits worked every scored body out again from the rows it wrote, but the light swing of a planet in a two-star system (flux_variation) was left as it was (NULL on a regenerated planet), so those scores read a stale swing. The edit writer now refreshes it from the final orbits first (insolation.refresh_system), as generation and the re-score do. test_admin_edit_scores.py proves that after each kind of edit the stored scores of every rocky body equal what store.refresh_habitability works out.

[8.0.2327] - 2026-10-25

Headline: A rogue planet now has a habitability score, so an ocean under its ice or under a hydrogen envelope is rated like any other world.

Changed

  • Rogue planets are scored (GEN.701, schema v158). A terrestrial rogue planet keeps the PHI-6 score and its six domain tiers, the four life scores, the four likelihoods behind microbial life, the survival equipment levels (eq_* and shelter_column_g_cm2) and the chemical energy (energy_flux_w_m2), worked out from its surface regime by planetgen/physics/rogue_habitability.py: the regime's gas, the water state (an ocean under ice, a hycean ocean, ice or none) and its water column, its own heat as the only energy, and the galactic cosmic-ray dose under its air plus the gamma dose of its crust. No life is drawn for a rogue planet, so its life scores are 0 and the score says what the surface would allow a visitor. There is no star, so no regional temperatures or hours outside are kept. The system page of a rogue planet shows the PHI-6 score; a gas giant and a brown dwarf have none.
  • Migration 0158, schema v158. rogue_planets gain 37 columns; a galaxy made earlier gets the same numbers from the surface its rows already hold (nothing is drawn). A generated rogue planet carries the score, so a rogue planet's output changes and the generator epoch is bumped.
  • The property sheet shows it. describe/sheet.py lists the score, the tiers, the life scores and the energy in the Habitability and Life groups of a rogue planet's sheet, and the shelter column beside them.

[8.0.2322] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The carbon and nitrogen a rocky planet's mantle holds now match what the Earth, Venus and Mars are known to hold, so worlds at the Earth's distance no longer start with hundreds of bar of nitrogen.

Changed

  • Dry-class carbon (GEN.813). The dry delivery class drew 0.6 weight percent CO2, sixteen times the carbon of the bulk silicate Earth, and a planet at the Earth's distance draws that class nine times in ten. The bracket is now 0.018 to 0.1 weight percent (the stored dry value to the wet High case of Ortenzi et al. 2020), whose middle is the Earth's 100 ppm of carbon.
  • Nitrogen per carbon (GEN.813). The bracket is 0.005 to 0.1 (it was 0.001 to 0.1), whose middle is the Earth's 0.02; the measured values for the Earth, the CI chondrites, Venus and Mars (Bergin et al. 2015) are inside it. Before, 37 percent of draws at the Earth's distance held ten times the Earth's nitrogen; now none do. Nothing in the generator draws the mixture yet (it waits on GEN.411 and GEN.422), so no stored value changes today.
  • A test of the Earth, Venus and Mars totals against the drawn inventory, three stand-in registry rows (GEN.725) and a design note (volatile-inventory-against-planet-totals.md).

[8.0.2321] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The sulfate and sulfide balance that decides how much of the sulfur a volcano gives stays in the air is built as a module; nothing calls it yet.

Added

  • Sulfur sink (GEN.815). physics/sulfur_balance.py splits the degassed sulfur between the air, a calcium sulfate sink and an iron sulfide sink by the redox of the gas, limited by the crust the volcanism built, and leaves in the air only what the sinks have not yet taken (rain-out over liquid water, sulfation on a dry surface) and what they cannot hold. It replaces the stand-in that kept 1e-5 to 1e-2 of the sulfur in the air of a wet world once the surface-air step uses it. Five stand-ins are in the registry (AM45 to AM49). The module is not called by the generator yet, so no generated value changes.

[8.0.2318] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The planet generator now has a model of the volatiles that late impacts deliver to a rocky planet and the air they blow away.

Changed

  • Impact erosion and late delivery (GEN.739). A new module (impact_history) takes the mass a rocky planet accretes after its giant impacts (0.7 percent of an Earth mass for the Earth, falling with mass), the water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen those impactors bring, and the air they erode, and returns what the air and the surface keep. It reproduces the Earth's nitrogen and ocean, Venus's nitrogen, and the result that late impacts alone do not make Mars thin. The supply law has a hook (impact_inventory) that turns the result into atoms per 100 g of mantle. Nothing in the generator calls it yet (it waits on GEN.411 and GEN.422), so no stored value changes today.
  • The nine new constants are in the stand-in registry (GEN.725) with their source tier and tweak level. The design note is docs/design/composition/impact-erosion-and-late-delivery.md.

[8.0.2317] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The redox of a rocky world's magma ocean now follows the published ranges: its spread grows with mass, it keeps rising above one Earth mass, and the later mantle is never more reduced than the ocean it came from.

Changed

  • Width and rise above one Earth mass (GEN.482b). The spread of the magma-ocean redox grows from 0.5 log units at 0.1 Earth masses to 0.9 at one (the Hirschmann 2022 and Deng 2020 ranges for the Moon, Mars and Earth), and the mean keeps rising by 1.0 per dex of mass up to 5.4 Earth masses, where the pressures of the published calculations end. Nothing in the generator draws the mixture yet (it waits on GEN.411 and GEN.422), so no stored value changes today; the first air of a heavier rocky world will be more oxidised than before once it does.
  • The later mantle (GEN.482b). Its mean is held at the Earth value above one Earth mass (no source goes further), and a body never moves to a later mantle more reduced than its own magma-ocean surface.
  • Rows a1 and a2 are listed as partly verified with their limits (GEN.482); row a3 is unchanged because nothing reads it for a body with an air.

Headline: A dry, frozen or hot world can now hold liquid water underground, which lifts its Water rating and lets microbes live there.

Changed

  • Aquifers (GEN.654, DB.92, schema v157). A rocky world or moon with no liquid at its surface keeps aquifer_depth_km and aquifer_thickness_km, worked out by physics/aquifers.py from its heat flow, its surface temperature and pressure, its gravity and the water left in its surface reservoir: the layer of its crust where the pores are open and the water is liquid and not hotter than life can use. A world with none, a gas giant and a galaxy made earlier keep NULL (migration 0156).

The water is a solvent for life (the Microbial score can rise, capped at abiogenesis, so Flora, Fauna and Sentient stay 0), the life sees the ground's dose and the chemical power of the heat flow, and the Water rung is Yellow when the layer starts within 5 km and Red when it is deeper. A world with an ocean at the surface has none. The property sheet lists both numbers.

[8.0.2304] - 2026-10-25

Headline: scripts/test.py checks MySQL, Redis and the test setup before a run, restarts a server that dies during it and carries on without redoing the tests that passed; full is no longer called the merge gate.

Added

  • A check before every run (TEST.376). scripts/test.py loads the PLANETGEN_TEST_* variables from /etc/profile.d/planetgen-test.sh when they are missing, starts MySQL and Redis when they do not answer, purges the MySQL binary logs when under 3 GB of disk is free, and checks argon2-cffi and playwright 1.56.0. What it cannot repair stops the run with PREFLIGHT FAILED: ... and exit 2. scripts/test.py env does only the check; --no-preflight skips it. Before this a database test with MySQL down was skipped, not failed, and a run without PLANETGEN_TEST_MYSQL_USER failed with DatabaseLoginError as the wrong account.
  • A watchdog during every run. MySQL and Redis are asked every 15 seconds. A server that is gone is restarted, the phase's pytest is stopped and started again without the tests that already passed (the progress log, as --resume does), up to 5 times a phase; the closing line says how many restarts there were. A server that cannot be restarted ends the run with FAIL and exit 3, and --resume continues it.

Changed

  • full is the end-of-version run, not the merge gate (TEST.372). The help of scripts/test.py and docs/reference/testing.md now say an ordinary merge needs a green changed run (finished with --resume after an interruption), and that the whole suite is for TEST.261, SEC.33 and GEN.301.

[8.0.2303] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The update reloads the web server more safely: it tests Apache's configuration first, covers gunicorn hosts, and checks the site answers.

Changed

  • update.sh reload (OPS.29). Apache is checked with apache2ctl configtest before it is reloaded, so a broken config leaves the running Apache serving; it is restarted only when the update just installed or enabled mod_wsgi (other modules load on a reload). The planetgen-gunicorn unit (Linux) and the launchd gunicorn daemon (macOS) are reloaded the same way, and /api/health must answer afterwards (PLANETGEN_HEALTH_URL sets another address). A failed step ends the update non-zero and prints the command to run by hand; nothing running prints the commands and ends zero. The docs (apache.md, the server checklist) say a reload aborts requests a mod_wsgi daemon is serving after about 4 seconds.

[8.0.2301] - 2026-10-25

Headline: An account can have a picture, and it may be a GIF, an animated GIF too, checked under frame and pixel caps and stored as a clean copy.

Added

  • Your picture (SEC.36). The account page has a "Your picture" section to upload or remove a PNG, JPEG, ICO or GIF, and the picture shows beside "Signed in as". POST /api/auth/avatar and DELETE /api/auth/avatar do the same for the API, and GET /api/auth/me returns the picture's address. Control schema v20 adds admin_users.avatar (the update adds the column).
  • The avatar rules. At most 1 MiB, 1024 by 1024 pixels a frame, 100 frames, and 16 million pixels over all the frames. A GIF or PNG with several frames stays animated with its durations and loop count. The upload is refused in a plain sentence when it is over a cap, is a bomb header, or is another format.

Security

  • A GIF is read only for an account picture, and never from the uploaded bytes. Pillow is told which four formats to try, the size is read from the header before anything is decoded, a decompression-bomb warning is an error, Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS is lowered to 25 million, and frames are unpacked one at a time under the caps. What is stored is Pillow's new encoding of the pixels, so comments, XMP, ICC profiles, EXIF and application extensions other than the loop block do not survive. It is served with its own content type and nosniff. The site logo, icons and preview picture keep the SEC.35 rule and still refuse a GIF.

Headline: A server with no timing history now shows a rough time left, labelled as a guess, instead of "estimating".

A run's time left, the banner's hours and the Generate page's whole-job bar said "estimating" until a first unit finished, and left a later stage out of the total. They now start from a rough guess: the stage's units over the workers the host can run at once (its cores and memory) at a default cost per unit. [8.0.2285] - 2026-10-25

Headline: The plan's "about N stars expected" for the massive-star and bright-star passes now matches what the passes place, and each unit line says the stars it expects.

Changed

  • The expected-stars count beyond the outline follows the density (GEN.398, bug). The count of stars a shell holds beyond the galaxy's outline (what the pass's log line, its progress bar and its ETA use) probed each group at two longitudes 180 degrees apart. On a two-armed spiral both land on the same phase of the arms, so a group's young stars came out twice, or none, of what the sampler draws: on the default galaxy the shells just past the outline were counted at 3,250 stars where the pass placed 1,853. A group is now sampled at 8 colatitudes and 2 radii of equal volume and 16 longitudes, so its count follows the density wherever the disc falls away across it. On the default galaxy (4e9 solar masses, seed 0123...) the massive-star pass logged 22,593 and placed 21,642 before; it counts 21,389 now, and the part beyond the outline matches the stars placed in each range of shells within 4 percent. The sampler was right and is unchanged: no star moves and no generator epoch is spent.
  • A unit line says the stars it expects, not its weight. The "unit 8 of 445, about 133 stars expected" lines gave the unit's weight, its stars plus a share for every band walked, so a unit that placed 19 said it expected 133. They give the stars the unit is expected to place.
  • Tests. The count beyond the outline matches a Monte Carlo of the density within 6 percent for six shells of the toy galaxy; a task's expected stars are its shells', the far shells' or the components' share, not its weight.

[8.0.2277] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The picture upload now reads only PNG, JPEG and ICO files, and Pillow moves to 13.0.0, which fixes 37 reported flaws in its image decoders.

Security

  • Pillow 12.3.0 to 13.0.0 in both lock files (SEC.34). pip-audit listed 37 advisories for 12.3.0, all fixed in 13.0.0 (TIFF, GIF and PPM decoders reading out of bounds, a zero-width PPM, PDF appends). Only the pillow pin moved in requirements.lock and requirements-server.lock; the picture tests and the lock tests pass on 13.0.0.

It used to let Pillow try every format it knows and reject all but three afterwards, so a TIFF, GIF or PPM header was parsed first. Image.open now gets formats= the three, so a file of any other kind is "That file is not a readable picture." and no other decoder runs. New cases in test_web_seo.py refuse a TIFF, a GIF and a PPM. [8.0.2276] - 2026-10-24

Headline: Every call to the API now leaves one line in the activity log with who made it, how it came in, the route and the HTTP response code.

Changed

  • Every /api/ request is logged (API.15). planetgen.log gets an API call line when the answer is ready: the account (the key's owner, the signed-in user, god for a command-line tool, or -), via= (key, session, anonymous, console), method, route, path, HTTP status, milliseconds, bytes in and out, the user agent and the API version the client sent. Keys, tokens, passwords and bodies are never written.
  • X-Request-Id. Each answer carries the request id that is in the log line; a client's own well-formed id is kept.
  • api_log.internal. The calls the web pages make in-process (about six per page view) are marked internal=1; setting this to off leaves them out of the log. Default all.
  • The command-line tools that lift a lockout, forget devices and reset two-factor write the same line with user="god" and via=console.
  • docs/reference/api.md and docs/reference/config.md describe the log; tests/test_api_call_log.py makes a call each way and checks the line.

Headline: Two small parts that let the generator call the atmosphere mixture draw are in: the description of a body it reads, and what an ocean takes out of the drawn air.

Added

[8.0.2269] - 2026-10-24

Headline: Cold icy worlds now trap gas in ice cages, and cold dry worlds can keep liquid brine below the freezing point of water.

Changed

  • Brine under the ice (GEN.762). A cold body with very little surface water melts the base of its ice at the eutectic of a perchlorate brine (198 to 236 K) instead of 273 K, so it can keep a liquid brine ocean under a thin lid or none, with that salt's water activity. generation-output: changed

Changed

It now reads one shell at a time and writes a block as soon as the shells have passed it, so what it holds is the blocks of the current block shell of each level.

They are now a step of their own ("Making the block light totals", bar over the units), with a log line before the scan, after it, before the levels above the units and about every 30 seconds (tuning.PROGRESS_LOG_SECONDS).

Fixed

[8.0.2260] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The Galaxy Map keeps its stars in one buffer that each node adds to as it arrives, and positions are exact however far from the galaxy's centre the camera is.

Changed

  • One star buffer, filled node by node (MAP.267). A node arriving writes its own stars at the end of the star buffer and a node leaving is cut out by moving the tail of the buffer into its place; the nodes already drawn are not touched, where every change of the view used to rebuild every star (static/starbuffer.js, SlotStore). The buffer doubles when it is full. A change of the star filters still starts it afresh.
  • Stars are placed relative to the eye (MAP.267). Each position is a high and a low float32 and the shader subtracts the camera's own pair, so a star keeps under a quarter pixel down to about 0.2 AU from the camera at any distance from the galaxy's centre (one float32 was a dozen pixels off a parsec away 260 kpc out). The old frame rounded to a whole parsec at the camera's target is gone. The other browser buffers (territory dots, superbubbles, rings, block prisms, the system view) are still absolute: they stay with MAP.240.

[8.0.2259] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The surface pressure of a rocky world now has a physical law behind it: how much gas its interior has delivered by its age and what the ocean and the carbonate-silicate cycle take back, calibrated on the Earth and checked on Venus.

Changed

  • The supply law of the surface pressure (GEN.726). physics/surface_pressure.py gives the pieces the pressure sum of GEN.422 will use: the share of the mantle's volatiles that the body's heat release has brought to the surface (degassed_share, the melt-processing picture of Tosi et al. 2017, one calibrated energy so that an Earth twin has the Earth's 1e22 mol of surface carbon), the gas mass and pressure of a degassed budget, and the CO2 pressure at which silicate weathering balances volcanic outgassing (carbonate_pco2_bar, the law and the ranges of Lehmer, Catling and Krissansen-Totton 2020, solved with the surface temperature as a function of the pressure). interior_heat.Heat also reports the heat the interior has released since the body formed (released_j). Nothing is wired into the generator yet (GEN.411 and GEN.422 do that), so no world changes. The design is docs/design/composition/surface-pressure-supply-law.md; the seven stand-in constants are registry rows AM27 to AM33.

[8.0.2258] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A world's air is now stored gas by gas in its own tables, so any gas of the gas table can be in an atmosphere and the balance gas of a giant (helium) or a hot world (sodium) is a stored gas like the rest.

Changed

  • The air moves to planet_gases and moon_gases (DB.71, GEN.424). The ten p_<gas>_kpa columns of planets and moons are gone. Each gas above zero is a row (the formula in the gas table and its partial pressure in Pa), the class's balance gas (helium, sodium, ammonia) included, so the rows add up to the surface pressure. Migration 0155 copies each row's ten partial pressures into the new tables and drops the columns (schema 155); a row made before it has no balance-gas row until the galaxy is regenerated. physics/atmosphere.py keeps the air as the body attribute gas_partials_pa; physics/mixture.py, physics/air_column.py, the habitability, class, radiation, hydrosphere and System Map code read it through atmosphere.gas_partials_pa / atmosphere.partial_kpa. The System Map's body rows and the describer carry the air by gas formula. Sodium has no Rayleigh cross section, so the air column leaves it out.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.2257] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The test gate runs the tests that start real queue workers one at a time and cuts its worker count to the memory and idle cores the machine has.

Changed

  • scripts/test.py runs three phases instead of two (TEST.344). The tests that need no browser and no real queue worker run on every core; the real_queue tests, which start real worker processes and read the shared queues by name (so two at once kill each other's workers, TEST.302), run on one worker; the browser tests run last on two. The phase lines show the new phase.
  • The parallel phases are capped by free memory and load. At the start of a phase the runner counts one worker per 1000 MB of available memory (browser workers 2500 MB) and, in the first phase, no more than the cores the load leaves idle, never fewer than one, and says so on the phase line when it cuts. A lane machine that runs other lanes' gates now gets fewer workers instead of timeouts and OOM kills. --worker-mb, --browser-worker-mb and --no-worker-cap tune or turn it off. [8.0.2255] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A planet past its star's runaway greenhouse limit while the star was young now loses water, and the limit itself depends on the planet's mass.

Changed

  • The runaway greenhouse limit depends on the planet's mass (GEN.639). orbits.runaway_greenhouse_flux and orbits.hz_limits take the three Kopparapu et al. 2014 sets (0.1, 1 and 5 Earth masses): a heavier planet keeps its water to a higher flux, so its inner edge is nearer the star. The star's own habitable zone and a planet's zone label are unchanged (the zone is needed before the planet's mass is known).
  • Early water loss (GEN.639). physics/runaway_history.py follows each rocky planet's and moon's flux from 30 Myr to its star's age, along the pre-main-sequence track and the star's rise to its present light, and where the flux is above the runaway limit it removes the water that the energy-limited escape of the steam takes (efficiency 0.01, the star's own XUV). hydrosphere.generate_hydrosphere takes the loss off the surface reservoir first, and volcanism returns 30 percent of the mantle's water, never more than was lost (the escape does not reach the mantle). The bulk water of the composition is unchanged: the loss is in the surface water, the oceans and their depth. A Sun-like star's zone loses nothing; only the worst red dwarf zones (the faintest stars and the inner edge) come out dry. Nothing new is drawn. Generator epoch bumped.

[8.0.2251] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The old queue executor is removed; nothing in a run used it any more.

Changed

  • The old work-queue executor is gone (OPS.66, Boss). WorkQueue, RQExecutor, RQFuture, Channel, _rq_task and the --debug FILE plumbing of that path had no caller in a run since runs became units queued by the wrapper; nothing is kept for compatibility. The job tree (job_node, the admin Queue page and API), worker_count and task_seed stay. The tests of the removed executor are removed with it, and the ones that only needed a queue node to look at use a plain job node.

[8.0.2250] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A Generate run no longer dies with "Execution not found in Redis" after its sectors are saved.

Changed

  • A new-galaxy run on a loaded server failed after saving its first sectors with ValueError: Execution ... not found in Redis (PERF.173, bug). A worker works out what a unit reads from the galaxy (PERF.146's warm) before it forks the unit's process, and it did that after RQ had created the unit's execution record, which expires 90 s after its last beat while the process's first beat comes 30 s after the fork. A warm of over a minute (five workers building the shape of a galaxy with 15,000 clusters at once) left a unit that finished within 30 s of the fork without its record, and RQ failed the finished unit when it cleaned up, which ended the run with its sectors saved. The worker now warms before the record is made. A unit that is already done when RQ fails it no longer fails the run or runs again, since its result is stored and counted. The note in the units' module that RQ calls on_failure only after the retry was wrong (RQ calls it on every failure); it now says what happens.

TODO items resolved: none. Added: none.

[8.0.2249] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A giant's layered interior is now saved with the world and read back with it.

Changed

  • Giant interior storage (DB.89): each giant planet and moon now keeps the kind of interior it was drawn with, its compact and dilute core masses, the pressure where its hydrogen turns metallic, its helium depletion and whether it has a helium shell, in new columns on the planet and moon rows. Its layers (kind, state, pressure and radius at the top and bottom, and the mass of each material) are saved one row per layer in two new tables, planet_interior_layers and moon_interior_layers. Worlds saved before this version have no interior until the galaxy is regenerated at the generator epoch. Database version 154.

[8.0.2248] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The Galaxy Map shows the light of the stars too far away to tell apart as a soft glow that turns into stars as you zoom in, and the Menu can switch it off.

Added

  • The unresolved glow (MAP.266). Each sector-block node lists only its brightest stars; the rest of its light, stored in its aggregate (the pre-placed stars nothing was built from and the generated sectors' total), is drawn as one soft blob at the centre of that light, in the color of its temperature, under the stars. A blob shows for the share the cut gives its node (galaxynodecut.weightCalculator), so as a block hands over to its children the glow gives way to their stars and blobs and the light is conserved: nothing pops and nothing doubles. static/galaxyglow.js chooses the blobs and how strongly each shows (a tone curve over its apparent magnitude, judged 5 magnitudes deeper than a point of light); static/galaxyglowlayer.js draws them as screen-sized quads. The Menu's "Show on the map" group has an "Unresolved glow" button (on by default; hide=glow in the address turns it off). The Sector Map has no glow.
  • A second warm-up over addressed sectors builds no answer (MAP.289: the bug does not reproduce; the test holds it).

[8.0.2247] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The gas giant density test no longer fails on about one run in six, and the slow scatter-pass tests get a timeout that fits a loaded machine.

Fixed

  • test_gas_giant_density_is_its_mass_over_its_volume failed in 7 of 40 runs, with or without load (the load flakes noted on TEST.344). Since GEN.460 a giant's radius comes from the interior tables, and a hot young giant swells past 1.3 times the median mass-radius relation (one draw gave 46,695 km against a 32,741 km ceiling), so the test's 3-sigma band around the median was wrong. The test now checks the radius stays in the class's radius range and that the density is the mass over the volume; the 60 reruns after the change all pass.
  • test_star_scatter_passes.py runs the 900 s default timeout close on a loaded machine. Its three scatter runs build the bright-star tables in pure Python (60 to 130 s alone), so the module now carries the same 3600 s timeout test_budget_queries.py uses. TODO items resolved: none (these are the two load flakes noted on TEST.344, whose own item is the serial browser phase). Added: none.

[8.0.2246] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The population model, the tuning table and the body-look pressure convert milliparsecs, megayears and pascals through the one unit registry, with the same numbers.

Changed

  • population/model.py (system and capital positions from milliparsecs to parsecs), tuning.py (the open-cluster age windows from megayears to gigayears) and web/maps/bodylook.py (pressure from pascals to kilopascals) call unit_registry.converter instead of a typed / 1000.0 (GEN.571, fifth file group). Each replaced expression gives the same float bit for bit, so no generated value moves. The web/maps/starmap.py sites use physics.units helpers and wait for the epoch-changing pass.

[8.0.2245] - 2026-10-24

Headline: Moons now have an origin, and a moon caught from elsewhere can orbit backwards or steeply tilted.

Changed

  • A moon draws how it came to orbit its planet, and its orbit follows from that (GEN.714). A giant planet's moon is a disk moon or a captured body, a terrestrial planet's an impact moon or a captured body, and a dwarf planet's a partner or a captured body, each with an equal chance because no source gives the shares. A regular moon lies within 25 degrees of its planet's equator as before. A captured moon takes any orbit outside the band between 55 and 130 degrees where such orbits are unstable, so it is either prograde or retrograde, about 43 and 57 percent. The origin is held while the system is generated and is stored once the composition columns (DB.70) exist.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.2244] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The mail server, the site's address and the From address now open only for the Owner, after typing the password again.

Added

  • The Owner account stub (USR.31). The account the install seeds is the Owner; python3 -m planetgen.cli.accounts --set-owner USER makes another account the Owner (the old one becomes an admin) if that one is lost. The control database gains admin_sessions.password_confirmed_at (control schema v19), set at sign-in and renewed by POST /api/auth/confirm-password.
  • Owner-only settings behind a recent password (ADM.86). An option marked Owner (the mail server, base_url, the From address) can be changed only by the Owner whose password was typed within the last 10 minutes, from a signed-in session (an API key is never more than an admin). Admins see those options disabled with the reason; the Owner whose password is older sees a panel that asks for it. GET /api/admin/settings adds reauth, and an option's fixed_kind can be reauth. Backup downloads follow the same role.

[8.0.2243] - 2026-10-24

Headline: How old a star must be to host a planet now depends on the planet's air, temperature and gravity, not on its class letter.

Changed

  • Age needs from conditions (GEN.686). The youngest a star can be and still host a planet or moon is read from the body's stored conditions (physics/age_needs.py, physics/data/age_needs.json) as one of five tiers (no settling time for giants, airless and small worlds; molten; settled; watered; frozen), each with its minimum age on a fast, normal or slow evolving star. The ages are the old per-class minimums, so about 99% of bodies need the same age as before and a few (some thin-air and cold worlds) need a different one. The age_ranges of every class in tuning.PLANET_CLASSES are deleted. generation-output: changed

[8.0.2242] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A real Stop everything: one button, one command and one update option end every run, queue and worker process on the server and keep it quiet until you resume.

Added

  • PERF.186: Stop everything. The admin Queue page has a Stop everything button (and planetgen queue stop-all the same on the command line). It cancels the Generate page's job and every live run, empties every queue, and ends every planetgen worker, job runner and command process on the server together with the processes they started. It also writes a hold that survives a restart of Redis, the web server and the host: while it is on, no worker, run, Generate job, orbital update or cache warm-up starts, the map queues no background work, and a banner on every admin page says so. Resume (the button, or planetgen queue resume) lifts it. It works when Redis is not answering.
  • PERF.186: ./update.sh --kill-all. Runs the same stop and clear before the update, only when you give it. It leaves no hold behind.

Fixed

  • PERF.186: Cancel left work running. A job whose runner had died (killed by the memory killer, a restart) showed as interrupted and Cancel did nothing, while its step and the processes of that step went on using the host. Cancel now ends them, cancels the job's runs and frees the job lock. A running step that ignores the request to stop (it caught the signal or hung in a database call) is now killed after 20 seconds.
  • PERF.185: the process list was read cut off to the terminal's width where the terminal sets one, so a worker whose command line was long could be missed by the host cap. It is now read in full, here and in the memory watch.

[8.0.2241] - 2026-10-24

Headline: Every Generate job log now says how much memory each step used, and a nightly small New galaxy run fails when a step uses far more than its budget.

Added

  • PERF.183: memory per step in every job log. While a Generate job runs, the job runner looks every two seconds at MySQL, the planetgen workers, the step's own processes and the whole host, and after each step writes one line to the job log ("Memory peak: MySQL 884 MB, 6 workers 2,310 MB, the step itself 256 MB, the whole host 3,100 of 15,990 MB.") and keeps the figures in memory.json in the job folder. The figures are proportional set sizes, so a work horse forked from its worker is not counted twice.
  • PERF.183: the nightly New galaxy smoke run. python -m planetgen.cli.smoke runs the real New galaxy job for one small neighborhood in scratch databases (dropped afterwards), prints the peaks of every step against their budgets (tuning.SMOKE_BUDGET_MB, or --budget GROUP=MB) and exits 1 when a step is over, 2 when a step failed. examples/maintenance/install-maintenance-timer.sh --with-smoke-timer installs a systemd timer for it at 04:30 every night, so a change that makes a step hold far more memory is caught the night it merges, not on the first big galaxy.
  • PERF.183: the first measured run found a hog. On a 12 pc neighborhood every step stayed under 1 GB (most of them under 300 MB in their own process) except the phenomena scatter, whose own process held 6.4 GB (host 8.7 GB). Its budget is set 1.4 times that so it cannot get worse until it is fixed; every other step is judged against about twice its measured peak.

[8.0.2230] - 2026-10-24

Headline: Neutron stars and black holes now have the accreting companions astronomers see: high-mass and low-mass X-ray binaries, microquasars, spider millisecond pulsars and compact triples, each with an X-ray luminosity under its Eddington limit.

Added

  • High-mass X-ray binaries. 40% of the compact companions of living massive stars accrete; 60% of those are Be/X-ray binaries (young systems only), the rest wind-fed supergiant binaries.
  • Low-mass X-ray binaries. 5e-5 of neutron stars and 1e-3 of black holes have a low-mass star on a tight orbit, and 1% of those accrete from a donor filling its lobe at a period of 4 to 24 hours.
  • Microquasars. One in ten accreting neutron stars and black holes launches jets (new member flag microquasar).
  • Spider millisecond pulsars. Recycled pulsars have black widow (6%), redback (3%) and other (2%) companions with the observed masses and periods of hours (new member flag ablating).
  • X-ray luminosity. A tree derives the luminosity of each accreting pair from the gas it captures, never above the accretor's Eddington limit.
  • Dormant companions and compact triples. Detached neutron star and black hole pairs with a star are listed as dormant (the Gaia kind), and 30% of neutron star and black hole binaries now have a third member (black holes only before).

Changed

  • Generated systems change. A neutron star or black hole pair no longer accretes by chance geometry; the recycled pulsar companion odds follow the registry classes. Every galaxy regenerates differently (generator epoch recorded).

[8.0.2224] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A planet's inner heat is now the heat its rock makes plus the heat it was born with, so a young world is much hotter than an old one and no longer a fixed share radiogenic.

Changed

  • Formation heat modelled (GEN.699). planetgen.physics.interior_heat follows a body's mantle from its making: it starts as hot as the energy of assembling the body allows (a magma ocean for a planet, cold for a planetesimal), then cools by convection through the mantle's boundary layer while its radioactive rock (the stored potassium, thorium, uranium and aluminium-26 of GEN.459) heats it. It is the stagnant-lid model of Guimond, Rudge and Shorttle 2022. The heat out is the radiogenic heat plus the cooling of the interior.
  • The Urey ratio is an output. It is no longer drawn between 0.1 and 0.9; it is the radiogenic share of the heat that comes out. An Earth-mass twin gives 27 to 37 TW and a ratio of 0.57 to 0.76 over the published range of mantle rheologies, and a body of 0.1 billion years gives four to thirty times more heat than at 4.5.
  • Stored (schema 153). planets and moons gain mantle_eta0_pa_s and mantle_activation_kj_mol (the two draws of the mantle's rheology) and internal_heat_flux_w_m2 (the heat flow at the body's surface); urey_ratio keeps its column and is now computed. NULL on rows made before this release.
  • The heat flow of every rocky planet, moon and rogue changes, and with it the ice shell, the ocean, the volcanism gate and the habitability score that read it.
  • Generator epoch bump (numbered at merge).

A galaxy run backfills dimmer bright stars around the sectors it generates, but that backfill skipped a sector that was already filled, so a sector generated before the backfill reached it held fewer systems than one the backfill reached first. [8.0.2221] - 2026-10-24

Headline: Where an atmosphere freezes out is now worked out from the checked saturation curves, so hydrogen sulphide, carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide land at the right temperatures.

Changed

  • The freeze-out cap reads the checked saturation curves (GEN.452). physics/atmosphere.py no longer carries the two-point condensation table, whose hydrogen sulphide row was a copy of sulphur dioxide's and which put carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide and the cold gases 2 to 20 K off. The most a gas can be vapour at the surface temperature is now its saturation pressure from physics/saturation.py (the Fray and Schmitt and laboratory solid curves, the Span and Wagner carbon dioxide curve, the Wagner liquid curves, nothing above the critical temperature). Hydrogen sulphide boils at 213 K at 100 kPa instead of 263 K, nitrogen at 37 K holds 1.2 Pa (Pluto's air) instead of 10 Pa, and the cold gases follow the laboratory curves of the cold ends. New saturation.condensation_temperature_k gives the inverse. The cloud condensation of physics/aerosols.py reads the same curves. Stored partial pressures and total surface pressures change for cold bodies.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.2220] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The server now refuses to run more worker processes than its memory and cores can hold, whatever starts them.

Added

  • PERF.185: a cap on all planetgen worker processes on one host. A start of a worker for any queue is refused once the host already runs queue.max_host_workers of them (0, the default, sizes it from the host: 60 percent of its memory in workers of 300 MB each, no more than four a core, never fewer than the cores plus four; a 16 GB, 8 core host gets 31). The count comes from the process list, so a worker still importing its libraries counts. The refusal is logged once a minute and counted, and the Queue page shows the cap, how many run and how many starts were refused in the last hour. This is the second guard behind PERF.181: even if something else starts workers in a burst, the host cannot be filled.

generation-output: changed

[8.0.2216] - 2026-10-24

Headline: A burst of map requests can no longer start over a hundred queue workers and run the server out of memory.

Fixed

  • PERF.181: the server ran out of memory and the kernel killed MySQL during a New galaxy run. Every Galaxy Map request that queues a tile asked the worker starter for upkeep workers, and requests arriving together each counted "none starting" before any of them recorded its own start, so each launched the whole set. On 2026-10-24 about 130 workers of 125 MB took all 16 GB of a host with no swap. Only one caller at a time now counts and starts the workers of a queue, and a started worker counts as starting for 90 seconds (it was 15) so a host that is slow to load a worker is not given a second one for the same need.

Added

  • scripts/enable-swap.sh makes a swap file (8 GB by default), switches it on and adds it to /etc/fstab so it stays on after a reboot; it does nothing when swap is already on. install.sh and update.sh warn when the host has no swap, and INSTALL.md has a Swap section and a requirements row.

[8.0.2215] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The Queue page lists the runs in Redis with their stages and time left, cancel stops a run at once, and a stuck run can be cleared.

Changed

  • The Queue page shows runs, not job trees (PERF.99). /admin/queue lists the runs in Redis newest first, each with its stage, how far it is, the time left and whether it has stopped answering. /admin/queue/<run id> shows one run's stages and the tail of its log, with cancel, clear and delete. The old job tree pages and the lease clear are gone; API version 6 (/api/admin/work returns runs, /log is new).
  • Cancel is instant (PERF.99). Cancelling a run takes its waiting units off the queue and sends the stop command to the started ones in one pass (0.1 s for 4,000 units), and the machine is free at once. A run that has stopped answering, or whose follower process is gone, can be cleared from the page.
  • Run logs are kept (PERF.99). Each run's event stream is written to runs/<run id>.log in the jobs directory when it ends, the last 20 kept, with a download link on the run's page.
  • The Generate page lists a job's runs (PERF.99). The job page has a Runs panel linking each run and its log, and Cancel job cancels the job's live runs at once instead of waiting for the step to notice.

[8.0.2214] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The chance that a planet is a water world now rises with its mass as in the Bern population synthesis.

Changed

  • Row b4 (GEN.510). The water-rich share depends on mass through the logistic fitted to the Bern synthesis (6.1 Earth masses is the centre), with a flagged plateau bracket of 0 to 1; it was a snow-line weight with no mass dependence. The comparison with the observed densities of M-dwarf planets is still open. The recipes are not read by the generator yet, so no generated value changes.

[8.0.2213] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The envelope rows of the atmosphere recipes are tuned to the observed radius valley.

Added

  • Rows e1 and e2 are tuned to the Kepler radius valley (GEN.509). A simulated Kepler survey (physics/radius_valley.py) reproduces the published valley slope (-0.11) and its radius at 10 days (1.84 Earth radii) along one degenerate ridge of the starting envelope and the loss efficiency; the rows draw on that ridge. Two new tuning targets. The recipes are not read by the generator yet, so no generated value changes.

[8.0.2212] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The database layer and the edit pages convert AU, km, years and parsecs through the one unit registry, with the same numbers.

Changed

  • db/store.py (the 67 AU-to-km and km-to-AU conversions of star, pair, comet and binary rows, the orbit clock and the SQL year constants), db/query.py, db/edits.py, db/precision.py, db/orbit_trees.py, db/point_columns.py, db/sector_paths.py, db/column_units.py and admin/edits.py call unit_registry.converter instead of a typed factor (GEN.571, fourth file group). Every replaced expression gives the same float bit for bit, so the stored values and the SQL text are unchanged. db/objectindex.KM_PER_LY is left for the epoch-changing pass: the registry's light-year-to-km factor differs from it in the last digit.

[8.0.2211] - 2026-10-24

Headline: The tide that heats an icy moon now feeds the ocean's life under its ice, so Europa- and Enceladus-like moons score on their real heat.

Changed

  • Tides in the chemical energy of an ice-covered ocean. hydrosphere.generate_hydrosphere kept the tide of an icy moon only long enough to thicken or thin its ice lid and then threw it away; the chemical energy term of the habitability score read the radiogenic heat alone, one to three orders of magnitude too low for a Europa or an Enceladus. The tide (tidal_flux_w_m2) is now kept on the moon, and habitability_world.generate adds it to the moon's own heat flow before the energy term (1 percent of the heat flow, as for any body).
  • Migration 0152, schema v152. planets and moons gain tidal_flux_w_m2 (DOUBLE, nullable; a planet keeps NULL). The forced eccentricity behind a tide is not stored, so a moon saved earlier keeps NULL and its energy flux; only a moon generated now has it. Generator epoch bumped.
  • A moved planet's moons are scored again (GEN.704). validation.reconcile_moved_planet refreshed a moon's air for its parent's new distance from the star but kept the dose, UV and habitability it had drawn at the old one; each moon that keeps its class now gets generate_spin, which ends with them, as a moved planet does.
