[8.0.1494] - 2026-10-16

Headline: Stars, black holes, neutron stars and planetary nebulae in the scatter now come with their companions.

Added

  • The scatter writes member trees (GEN.262). The mass pass, the luminosity pass, their backfills and the phenomenon pass give each placed object that has company its stars, brown dwarfs, white dwarfs, neutron stars and black holes in scatter_members and scatter_nodes, with the row's member_count and system_mass_solar set (the row's point is the system's barycentre). A star row always draws its tree. A stellar black hole has a companion 1.25% of the time (a star 1.0%, a black hole 0.2%, a neutron star 0.05%), an intermediate-mass black hole a star 1%, a neutron star and a planetary nebula's central white dwarf at their tables. The tree is a function of the row's seed alone, and its nodes' phases are stamped with the orbit epoch (a fixed origin before any orbit update), so two scatters with the same seed store the same members. planetgen plan says how many of the stars and phenomena it placed have companions.

Changed

  • The black-hole and neutron-star rates are rates of rows. A row is a system keyed by its placed object, so a class's object rate is divided by one plus the same-class companions per row (1.002 for a stellar black hole), which keeps the density of the class. Seeded scatters therefore differ from before by about 0.2% of their black holes.
  • Deleting scatter rows deletes their members. Clearing a scatter, one star pass, an unfinished band or the unbuilt stars of a cell takes the rows' members and nodes with them.
  • A pre-main-sequence member's state is PMS, which fits the 16-character column (the first tree to be written exposed that pre-main-sequence did not).

[8.0.1484] - 2026-10-16

Headline: The orbital update does nothing while an update is running, and a cancel never leaves positions half moved.

Changed

  • The orbital update refuses to run during an update. python -m planetgen.cli.orbits (the nightly timer, a Generate job's step, a queued run) checks whether an update is running, or has left the site closed after failing, before it touches the database. If so it moves nothing, leaves every epoch, due time and the clock as they were, says why and exits with status 75 so the next timer firing simply tries again.
  • A cancel finishes the update of the positions first. Once the first stage has begun, a stop request (the update's cancel, Ctrl+C) lets the run finish moving, refiling, refreshing containment, nearest systems and sector paths and recording the clock, then exits, so stored positions are never left half moved. A cancel before anything moved stops at once, and a second Ctrl+C stops it regardless.

[8.0.1483] - 2026-10-16

Headline: Before an update changes anything it lists the running and queued work and stops unless you agree to cancel it, and nothing new can start while it runs.

Changed

  • update.sh lists the work that runs first. A Generate job, a planetgen run from the command line, jobs on the shared queues, an orbital update and a Galaxy Map warm-up are printed with their kind, id, start time and what they hold. On a terminal the update asks before cancelling them; with no terminal (a timer, cron) it refuses with a non-zero exit and changes nothing unless you pass --cancel-running. A migration run by hand (python -m planetgen.cli.migrate) does the same when it has something to migrate.
  • Cancelling goes through each job's own cancel path and the update waits for it. Queued jobs are removed, running ones are stopped so they end as cancelled, not failed, and the update starts only when none is left. A job that does not stop within 10 minutes is reported and the update stops before it has changed anything.
  • Nothing new can start while the update runs. The Generate page and the API refuse to queue work and say that the site is being updated, a command-line run that would open a job tree is refused, and the queue's workers exit with status 75. The Galaxy Map warm-up and the orbital update register themselves so a later update can see them.

[8.0.1482] - 2026-10-16

Headline: The site is closed for visitors (maintenance mode) while an update runs, and opened again when it has finished.

Changed

  • update.sh closes the site before it changes anything. It turns maintenance mode on (cause "update") and takes a lock, so visitors see the "being updated" page instead of pages that hang while a migration holds the database. A good update opens the site again at its end. If you had closed the site yourself, it stays closed afterwards, and a sector-grid conversion keeps it closed until the new Galaxy Map is built, as before.
  • A failed update leaves the site closed and says why. The message names the step that failed and the command that opens the site again (python -m planetgen.cli.maintenance off), because the database may be half migrated. The lock is released so ./update.sh can simply be run again.
  • A migration run by hand is guarded the same way. python -m planetgen.cli.migrate closes the site while it has something to migrate and opens it when done; with nothing to migrate it changes nothing.

The halo's stars are the halo term's; the cluster's density is 0 until the cluster components arrive (GEN.237). Migration 0094 lets bright_stars.population hold them.
  • The default galaxy's edge moves in by two shells (3,764 to 3,762) because the Sun's density of 1.0 now counts the halo.
  • The Galaxy Map's density mirror carries the halo term. The normalisation to the local density (about 2.7 times higher) is kept as tuning.HALO_LOCAL_DENSITY_FRACTION.

Headline: Every object now has a 96-bit ID, every scatter point moves with the galaxy, and the grid reaches 262 kpc.

  • The nightly orbit update moves every scatter point (GEN.223): bright stars and every kind of phenomenon scatter (the nucleus stays at the center). Points on the rotation curve turn about the galactic axis, hypervelocity stars fly a straight line, and a point that crosses a cell boundary is refiled there. Each point keeps its position, velocity, epoch_unix and next_update_due in its own columns.
  • New tables scatter_members and scatter_nodes hold a multi-star point's members and orbit tree (GEN.260), with the columns the system-type catalogue needs (member state and flags, node interaction, a group's offsets and velocities, up to 12 members), and the scatter rows carry member_count and system_mass_solar; the point is the barycentre.
  • Every table that holds a point in the galaxy frame gets a cell_key (DB.34, DB.35): a generated column with the Morton key of the object's 0.25 pc cube, and a covering index (cell_key, x, y, z), the base of the region queries. A star system also keeps its point in the galaxy frame (galaxy_x/y/z_pc) now, since its own position is relative to its sector. galaxy/cellkey.py is the same function in Python.

[8.0.1417] - 2026-10-16

Headline: The whole planetGen install belongs to the web user (www-data:www-data), set the same way by install.sh and update.sh, and the example Apache2 site refuses to serve anything but the app and static files.

Changed

  • examples/apache/set-permissions.sh now takes the checkout (and optionally a state folder) instead of src/html and db: it gives everything in it to Apache's user and group, directories 750, files 640, scripts and *.py 750 (files that already have the owner execute bit keep it), makes /var/lib/planetGen/state if it is missing, and never follows a symbolic link. install.sh and update.sh both call it on the whole checkout, so a fresh install and an update end with the same ownership. The virtual environment and the NLTK corpus stay root's, because the root-run scripts execute that Python.
  • update.sh trusts its own checkout for git (it is no longer root's), and says when an update changed examples/apache/planetgen.conf.example or examples/redis/planetgen.conf, with the diff command to compare. It still never edits your Apache site or your Redis config.
  • examples/apache/planetgen.conf.example denies the whole install tree (no listings, no handlers, AllowOverride None), lets back in only wsgi.py and static/, and refuses source, configuration, state, logs, .git, dotfiles and the virtual environment by name even if a later Alias points at them. Update your own site file by comparing it with the example.

Fixed

  • A web process can write its own state folder on a fresh install as well as after an update (the maintenance flag could not be written when the install tree belonged to root).

Compact pairs that would already have merged are rejected, and a bound companion beyond 1,000 AU of a neutron star or a black hole that did not collapse directly is rejected.

[8.0.1396] - 2026-10-15

Headline: Working out the path of a body held by a heavy black hole no longer takes minutes in a core sector.

Changed

  • A body held by a heavy mass (the thousands of rogue planets that orbit a core black hole) used to run all 20,000 integration steps of its sector path, about half a second each, so a core sector with a 10 to 90 million solar-mass hole took many minutes to settle and test_galaxy_gen timed out about one run in three (GEN.232). A path is now cut off once its direction has turned through one full revolution (sector_path.MAX_TURN_RAD), the most the spline's 48 knots can follow anyway, and the hard step ceiling is 2,000. A held body now costs about 5 ms, whatever the hole's mass, and every body's cost is bounded the same way. Paths that leave the sector are unchanged to the last bit. The integrator also visits the point masses once per step instead of twice (sector_path._pull).

TODO items resolved: GEN.232. Added: none.

[8.0.1346] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Wide binaries keep both stars' orbit regions apart (GEN.228). Each star's stable limit is now the tighter of the Holman & Wiegert fit and its own Hill sphere in the pair at periapsis (orbits.hill_radius_in_pair_au), the clearance between the two stars' outermost planets is measured at the pair's closest approach, not its average separation, and every comet a wide binary's star gets is an elliptical one whose whole orbit stays inside that limit (re-rolled up to COMET_CEILING_ATTEMPTS times, dropped when none fits). Before, comets ignored the limit: with comets forced on, 1,266 of 1,500 generated wide binaries had a comet reaching past it, toward the companion's planets.
  • validation.check_star_system reports a comet that leaves its star's stable limit, and stabilize_star_system with removal drops it.
  • planetgen check-db --deep --wide-binaries validates only the wide binaries, to count the stored pairs that break the rule.

[8.0.1343] - 2026-10-15

Added

  • Maintenance mode: while it is on, every page and API call answers "being updated" (a page at /maintenance, a JSON 503 from /api) to anyone but a signed-in admin or an admin's API key; sign-in and static files stay reachable. It is one file (maintenance.json beside settings.json), switched from the admin page or python3 -m planetgen.cli.maintenance on|off|status. The site is open in its normal state: planetgen.cli.migrate turns it on before it converts a database to the spherical sector grid, and the map rebuild turns it off with maintenance.turn_off_for(maintenance.SECTOR_SWITCH).

Changed

  • The API, the web pages and the Generate page speak the spherical sector grid: sectors are addressed by shell, band and wedge (/api/galaxy/cell, /api/galaxy/bright-stars and /api/galaxy/uncharted take ?shell=&band=&wedge=, /api/galaxy/shape returns shells), the Generate page's modes are random start, a whole shell, around a sector, one address and a span of shells, bands or wedges, and the sector page and nav chart show the new address.
  • The Galaxy Map redirects to the maintenance page while maintenance mode is on, and shows a notice in place of the map when it is off but the new map has not landed; the Sector Map shows the same notice.

Removed

  • The Generate page's whole-ring, column and Galaxy Map block modes, and the radius-in-sectors cylinder fields.

[8.0.1342] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Generation runs on the shell grid: regions and spans are shells, bands and wedges (galaxy/region.py, span.py); the bright-star and phenomenon scatters draw one shell at a time from a stream of their own, each band with its own density bound (object_first.band_majorants); the nebula field's extent comes from the outline (nebula_field.field_extent_pc).
  • planetgen galaxy takes --shell I (with --band J and --wedge K for one band or one sector), spans --shells/--bands/--wedges, and random starts --max-shell; plan takes --max-shell; fingerprint and check-db take --shell. limits.MAX_GENERATE_SHELL replaces MAX_GENERATE_RING. The cylinder fill (--cylinder-sectors, --cylinder-layers), --column, --block-layer, --ring, --layer, --slot, --rings, --layers, --slots and --max-ring are gone; --block is refused until the Galaxy Map's ladder is rebuilt on shells (MAP.205).
  • The neighborhood fill is a ball: ADM.30's "cylinder height = X layers" no longer applies.

  • Every species now has environment limits: the human habitability table with some rows replaced, made from its homeworld so a species always passes its own homeworld. The six habitability domains can be scored against a species' limits, and a species' limits show on its page (POP.12).
  • Lists of what could live where: the species that could live on a planet or moon (unaided, or with equipment their tech level can make), the worlds of a system or sector one species could live on, a "Species that could live here" panel on the system page, and API routes for each. The limits are generated from the homeworld until DB.30 adds the columns to store them.

Fixed

  • The system page no longer answers 404 when the API says there is no owner, facility types or species list to show; its tests now fake those calls.

[8.0.1284] - 2026-10-15

Added

  • A run now has one record in Redis: its stages, how many units each has finished, an event stream that serves as the live log, and an estimate of the time left. When a phase reports no updates, the estimate comes from earlier runs' stage timings, or from the time per task so far in this run, so the whole bar always shows a time remaining.
  • A public view of the active run (stage, percent, time left, whether the time comes from earlier runs) for pages to show.

[8.0.1251] - 2026-10-15

Added

  • Facility types and typed fields. An admin can define facility types (a name, a kind, an icon, a description) with up to 24 typed fields each (whole number, decimal, text, yes/no or one of a list), through GET/POST /api/facility-types, PATCH/DELETE /api/facility-types/<id> and the matching /fields routes. Anyone can read them. A type facilities use keeps its kind and can only be retired, and a field with stored values cannot change under them (POP.10).
  • Type, affiliation and ratings on facilities. A facility can take a type with that type's field values, an affiliation (a polity, whose name it keeps, or free text) and Green, Yellow or Red ratings for crime, housing, resources, maintenance and health, set on POST /api/facilities or changed with the new PATCH /api/facilities/<id>. GET /api/facilities lists facilities and filters them by kind, type, affiliation and any rating, worst first if asked (POP.10).
  • Suggested ratings and an example type. POST /api/facilities/<id>/suggest-ratings (and one for every facility with an unset rating) fills the ratings nobody set from the host's habitability, the affiliated species' tech indices, the kind of facility and the distance from the capital, marks them generated and never changes a rating that is set. POST /api/facility-types/examples adds an example "Research outpost" type (POP.10).

[8.0.1220] - 2026-10-15

Added

  • scripts/test.py <command> --resume continues a run that was killed or stopped (TEST.151). With the same build id (same code and files, packages, Python, MySQL and Redis versions, command and day) it skips the tests that passed in the earlier run and runs the rest. It says RESUMING first and (RESUMED build ...: N more passed ...) on its last line, runs nothing and exits 2 if the build changed (naming the parts that did), and never stores its short duration as the command's usual time. An interrupted run's last line now says how many tests had passed and that --resume continues it.

[8.0.1182] - 2026-10-15

Added

  • An ocean moon has an induced magnetic field (GEN.178). A moon with a liquid ocean (an ocean under ice, a surface ocean or a Hycean one) now answers its parent planet's changing magnetic field with an induced dipole, the way Europa and Callisto do. The size comes from the parent's field at the moon's orbit, the period at which the moon sees it turn, and the ocean's depth and conductivity by ocean class; a Europa-like moon of a Jupiter-like planet gets about 100 nT at its equator. It is stored on the moon beside its own magnetic moment (induced_moment_a_m2, 0 for a moon with no ocean, a locked parent or no parent field). Moons generated before this release have none until they are regenerated.

[8.0.1178] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Nebula sizes from their stars (GEN.150). An emission, cluster or reflection nebula (classes C to G) now has an age, a list of host stars and, when it is ionized, a photon rate, and its radius and density follow from them (a Stromgren sphere grown as the front expands for the nebula's age) instead of being drawn on their own. A star hosts a nebula only while its birth cloud lasts: the star's age must be under the class limit (1 Myr for C, 10 for D, 20 for E, 50 for F, 5 for G), so old O stars light nothing. The odds are now 0.25 for O and B0 to B2 stars, 0.05 for B3 to B9 and 0.01 for A, and B0 to B2 stars no longer make D nebulae. D and E add a cluster drawn from the IMF. Nebulae stored before this release keep their sizes.

[8.0.1166] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Six habitability domains and Suitability (GEN.207). The habitability colours now run over six domains: Pressure, Temperature, Air (is the air breathable), Water (is the water drinkable; a world with no liquid water is Red), Radiation and a new long-term Suitability, the lowest of water within reach, native food and shelter from radiation. The overall score is the geometric mean held under colour gates: Radiation and Temperature cap it at their own colour, Pressure in Yellow or Red caps it there unless a full suit is needed anyway, Air, Water or a Red Suitability cap it at Yellow (never lower on their own), and Blue needs all six Blue. A Red Suitability is forced when Radiation, Temperature, Pressure or Water is Red. Planet and moon rows, the Habitability levels page and the description show all six; the equipment still comes from pressure, temperature, air and radiation. Scores stored before this release change when a planet is regenerated.

A small, iron-rich planet (0.05 to 0.1 Earth masses, like Mercury) was always given no field, because the dynamo-lifetime test ran before the rule that gives it Mercury's 3e19 A m2 dipole. The rule now runs first, so such a planet has a field at any age. Fields stored before this release change when a planet is regenerated.

[8.0.1150] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Stagnant-lid dynamos (GEN.177). A rocky planet's magnetic dynamo now lasts 0.4 as long unless it has plate tectonics (a mobile lid). Only a planet with a liquid surface ocean can: from half an Earth mass up it has a 0.6 chance (0.3 above five Earth masses, where the literature is split), and every other rocky planet (dry, ice-covered, vapour, Hycean) is stagnant like Venus and Mars. A watery Earth-mass world still keeping its field at 4.5 Gyr falls from about 38 in 100 to about 22; a dry one never does. Fields stored before this release change when a planet is regenerated.

[8.0.1149] - 2026-10-15

Fixed

  • The gravity/pressure correlation test no longer fails on a thin sample (TEST.149). test_atmospheric_pressure_correlates_positively_with_gravity asked for a positive Pearson correlation from 40 planets per class, but that correlation is about 0.10 with a spread of 0.04, so it was zero or less in about one run in a hundred on random draws and passed when run alone. It draws 320 per class (spread 0.017, nearly 6 standard deviations from zero); the docstring now gives the measured numbers.

[8.0.1146] - 2026-10-15

Added

  • A big-galaxy query budget tier: scripts/test.py budget (TEST.133). It builds, once and keeps, a database of 2,000,000 systems and 150,000 sectors by cloning one real saved system, runs the Systems and Sectors page and count queries on it, and fails a page that reads far more rows than it shows (counted from the server's own read counters, so the result does not depend on the machine). It is opt-in and not part of the merge gate or CI. Known slow pages are expected failures that name the item that fixes them. A 3,000-system version of every case runs in the ordinary suite so the tier does not rot.

Changed

  • scripts/test.py ends every run with one clear line: PASS, FAIL (with the test counts) or INTERRUPTED. A run that stops without any of the three was killed. docs/testing.md says to start long runs in the background with a timeout of at least 90 minutes.

Fixed

  • Two tests that failed on some random draws, not on load (TEST.147, TEST.149). test_only_due_planets_and_moons_move_and_count expected every moon of a random system to be due after one year, but a small moon far from its planet (about 50 years per orbit at 770,000 km) needs longer than a year to move 100,000 km; 2.7% of random systems have one. The test now expects exactly the bodies whose update interval is within the year and checks the others did not move. The nebula field table tests drew a random galaxy seed per database, and about one in sixteen seeds has no class M or N cloud reaching the sampled sectors; they now use a fixed seed.

[8.0.1145] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Habitability follow-ups (GEN.148). A person's radiation tiers now run Blue to 20 mSv/yr, Green to 100 mSv/yr, Yellow to 1 Sv/yr and Red beyond (they were 50 mSv, 100 mSv and 10 Sv), which closes the gap the research found between 100 mSv/yr and 10 Gy/yr; 50 mSv/yr stays the single-year limit. L_rad now reads absorbed dose in Gy/yr (3.06 Sv per Gy, from Mars's 0.236 Sv/yr in 0.077 Gy/yr) instead of treating Sv and Gy as equal. PHI_bio is now the Liebig blend of its four likelihoods (the weakest term to the power 0.65 times the geometric mean to the rest) instead of their product, so ocean worlds score nearer the research's table; a planet of a pulsar, neutron star or black hole is still rated lifeless (10 kGy/yr, Deinococcus's D10). A new harshness number (0 to 1, 0.5 for an unscored body) is ready for the tech draw. The design note carries the recomputed worked examples and the microbe dose figures. Scores stored before this release change when a planet is regenerated.

[8.0.1127] - 2026-10-15

Fixed

update.sh no longer stops at "Migrating the configured MySQL database" with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'is_auth_switch_request'". pymysql 1.2.3, the current release, fails that way when a MySQL 8 account (caching_sha2_password) logs in the first time after a server start on a server without TLS; the fix is merged upstream but not yet released, so planetGen now logs in through pymysql's own step with the one-line difference described in planetgen/db/login.py. The library check now requires pymysql 1.2.3 or newer, and a failed login prints "Couldn't log in to the database server at host:port as 'user'" with what to check, from every command (OPS.49).

[8.0.1123] - 2026-10-15

Changed

  • Every Redis connection (the web pages, the API's queued jobs, the tile locks, the login lockout store and the work queue) now comes from one client module with a connect and read timeout, a retry after a dropped connection, a health check and keepalive, so a hung Redis fails a call instead of hanging the web thread that made it.
  • The Generate page's jobs, the API's queued jobs and the scatter's progress messages travel through Redis as JSON instead of pickle. A run's own task queue still uses pickle until the work queue rebuild. planetgen.cli.worker now serves the web queue by default and refuses to mix the two kinds of queue in one worker.

The between-test reset of the shared rate limiter deleted every limiter key on the Redis server when the limiter used Redis, so test_ratelimit_redis.py lost half its counts whenever another worker ran at the same moment; it now resets only a limiter that counts in memory.

A scatter writes it with each row; planetgen plan --fill-map-luminosity fills it, resumable and in batches that never block readers, for a galaxy scattered before (DB.23, GEN.201).

[8.0.1106] - 2026-10-14

Fixed

  • A queued API job is no longer left waiting on a worker that was killed. The count of workers serving the queue came from a list only a worker's own start-up cleans, so a worker killed with kill -9 (or by the out-of-memory killer) stayed counted, and with a cap of one nothing replaced it. The count now drops entries whose worker is gone and counts only a worker whose process still runs on this host; a replacement starts and the queued job runs. A job a killed worker was running is still noticed after RQ's heartbeat runs out (about 90 s) and then runs again.

Fixed

  • The System Map's "Start Here" and "End Here" buttons were missing from every body's info panel (TEST.125, NAV.50). systemnav.js only accepted an object reference made of digits (moon:40), and since API.23 a body's reference is its printed ID (moon:0008000000-4000000-00D), so the buttons were dropped for every body. It now accepts the printed ID. The three browser tests that caught it (test_system_map_selection_drill_and_measure, test_system_page_3d_view_draws_switches_scale_and_keeps_the_diagram, test_a_body_link_opens_highlights_and_selects_it) now match the printed ID as well.
  • The orbit update stored a time up to half a second ahead on MySQL 8.4 (TEST.129): the column holds whole seconds, MySQL 8.4 rounds a fraction up where MariaDB drops it, and the next run read a clock that had gone backwards. finish_orbit_update drops the fraction itself, so both servers store the same second.
  • Test fixes: the Phenomena table fixture's fake get_systems takes the keyset after argument (TEST.142); the installer test pins which checkout planetgen imports from, so it passes from a git worktree (TEST.143); the comet position test builds a system with comets by construction and a second test compares the generated and scene positions of 4,000 comets of both orbit types (TEST.130, not reproduced in 400 random systems and 60,000 comets, so it stays open until it recurs).

[8.0.1057] - 2026-10-14

Changed

  • A round region is now one description of layer, ring and slot-arc ranges (MAP.151, first part). The cylinder the radial fills cut (--cylinder-sectors, the Generate page's "radius (sectors)") is planetgen/galaxy/region.py: the layers either side of the centre's, the rings the circle reaches and, in each ring, one arc of slots that may wrap past slot 0 or be the whole ring. The fills read it instead of walking a sphere round the centre and discarding what falls outside the can, so a wide fill near the axis costs a few steps a ring. Its count is instant and it converts to the Span ranges the span fills use and to the two BETWEEN ranges SQL needs where an arc wraps. The sectors a fill picks are unchanged.

[8.0.1049] - 2026-10-14

Changed

  • The Galaxy Map's tiles are sent packed (MAP.159). A tile was JSON, about 150 bytes a star (28 gzipped). It is now a packed tile, 20 bytes a star (about 12 gzipped): positions as 16-bit steps inside the tile's own span, luminosity, temperature and radius as log codes, the star class as its letter, and the id as a number or a printed ID. Clouds and point objects stay JSON inside the tile. The tile cache stores the packed bytes (.bin files) and /galaxy/tiles sends them one after the other behind a small JSON header, as application/vnd.planetgen.tiles; the example Apache and nginx configs compress that type. The browser keeps the packed bytes in its IndexedDB store (about seven times more tiles in the same space) and reads them with static/tilepack.js. The cache stamp changes with the release, so every cache refills once. A star's position is exact to under a hundredth of a pixel at the zoom its tile is used, its luminosity to 0.06%, its temperature to 2% and its radius to 4%. The page now reads charted where a star's system_id was.

[8.0.1048] - 2026-10-14

Changed

  • Retired MAP.154 from the roadmap.

[8.0.1047] - 2026-10-14

Changed

  • A Galaxy Map tile's bright-star list now holds every star its parent listed inside it (MAP.154). The lists used an equal share per population and three height bands, so a child tile could drop a star its parent showed, and the zoom fade had to cover for it. Every tile level now ranks the pre-placed bright stars by one key, luminosity times a population weight (young 1, intermediate 10, old and bulge 400, so an old giant at 2,500 Lsun ranks beside a young star at a million), and a tile inside another lists all of the outer tile's stars in its box. The rank fade is now exact. Old giants still appear, but a crowd of young stars of high enough luminosity can now outrank them in a tile.

[8.0.1037] - 2026-10-14

Changed

  • numba is now a required library, installed by install.sh and update.sh with the rest of the NumPy stack; there is no pure-Python fallback. The minimum Python becomes 3.12 (it was 3.9, and 3.10 on macOS), the README, INSTALL.md and the lock files say so, and CI no longer runs a Python 3.9 leg (the MySQL 8.0 leg runs on 3.12). The website itself never imports numba, because numba's default cache needs a writable code or home folder that Apache's web user lacks; a test keeps it that way.

The translucent blocks along a line of sight used to add up (a ray through twenty 30% faces is over 99% opaque). Their faces and lines are now drawn at a share worked out from the stage's cells and the way the camera looks, so the blocks along any ray add up to no more than half, and the lines between slabs are fainter. The near-field window now thins only the blocks' density and cell boxes; a star is never faded by it, so stars stay visible in the middle of a filled block and in front of the camera, and a star close to the line to the focus can be picked. The window's edge is wider and shallower (it never fades below a quarter), which removes the visible rim around it.

The phenomena scatter also records how much of each layer's time went into writing its rows ("Phenomena layer: writing the rows"), the rest being the drawing. Speeds recorded before this are not carried over: the first scatter on a server starts its bars from the layer count alone.

[8.0.1029] - 2026-10-14

Changed

  • A binary pair is drawn in the same place on the Galaxy Map and the Sector Map (MAP.186). The Galaxy Map's tiles added a system's stored offset to its sector's centre as if it were already in the galaxy's axes, but the offset follows the sector's own axes, which the Sector Map rotated into place; every generated star in a tile was therefore off from where the Sector Map put it, a pair most visibly. Tiles now rotate the offset the same way, the nearby search measures from the same real place, and a pair's second star sits its real separation from the first by one rule used in both maps. The Sector Map still draws a close pair's two dots apart so they read as two (their real gap is far too small to see at that scale), and says so in its help and in its scene data (binariesCompressed); /sector/<id>/scene?binaries=real draws them at their real gap.

It prints the start time and how long the same command took last time on this checkout.

  • Failures are kept and re-run alone (.test-failures.jsonl): every failing test's full report with the worker and the machine's load, and when the run ends the failed tests run again alone with the verdict "passes alone" (a load failure) or "FAILS ALONE" (a real one). quick takes 2 min 33 s for 11,545 tests.

[8.0.975] - 2026-10-11

Changed

  • A Galaxy Map tile whose slowest piece times out is shown without it and fetched again, not replaced by the "Took too long" page (PERF.76). A tile is eight separate reads; each now runs under its own 3-second limit. A tile that lost a piece is sent marked incomplete, is not kept in the tile cache or the browser's store, and the map asks for it again after 5, 10 ... 30 seconds (six times at most) while the database catches up.
  • Counts nobody has stored stop at 10,000 (PERF.77). The Systems and Sectors tables used to count up to 50,000 rows when no stored count existed for a filter. They now count to 10,001, which takes 30 ms where a full count took 6 s, and show "10,000+" until the exact figure arrives. The API sends total_capped: true.
  • The Systems table pages forward by key (PERF.75). GET /api/systems?after=<system ID> starts after that system in the name sort, and the table sends the previous page's last system, so a page far down costs what page 1 does (page 1,500,000 took 8.5 s by OFFSET, 2 ms by key). Jumping straight to a distant row with the scroll bar still skips rows the old way; a jump-by-letter box is not built yet.

Added

The first report, docs/design/generation-benchmark-report.md, finds two workers making the plan's scatter 12 times slower, saving sector paths costing a quarter of a small fill, and the neighbour search making 1.8 million distance calls.

[8.0.940] - 2026-10-11

Changed

  • The Systems and Sectors tables no longer count their whole table on every page load, and a busy database fails gently (PERF.64). Each load of the Systems list ran four full scans of the systems table (about 3 s per million systems each), so a big galaxy, or any fill, pushed it past the 10 s limit. The totals and filter menus are now stored counts, made by one background count at a time (not sooner than every 30 s, or three times as long as the last one took), with the last count served while a new one is made and an estimate before the first. A statement stopped by the time limit is named in the activity log (DB statement_timeout, with its SQL and seconds). The 504 page now says the database is busy, reloads itself every 10 seconds and sends Retry-After, the API's QUERY_TIMEOUT carries Retry-After too, and the Galaxy Map asks again after 2, 4, 8 ... 30 seconds when a tile request fails instead of waiting for the next camera move. The Systems list stops using DISTINCT where no star join can repeat a row, and the search page's cache key no longer counts every sector.

[8.0.939] - 2026-10-11

Changed

  • The Galaxy Map draws a star at an opacity that follows its apparent magnitude from the camera (MAP.148): the limit is chosen each time the view changes so about 20,000 stars show (8,000 on a phone), counted among the stars actually on screen, so a packed core shows fewer faint stars and thin space more, and a star's core brightens or dims with its flux. The limit never dims a star at the distance you are looking at, only those much farther away, and it eases rather than jumps. Black holes, neutron stars and quasars always stay lit. The server's per-level luminosity floors stay as they are for now.

A job whose worker was just exiting is picked up by the next status read.

When the camera is inside a block, that block is drawn from the inside (faint walls and edges). Picking agrees with drawing: a block faded below a share of 0.35 can't be picked, so a click goes through to what is behind it, and the walls of the block you are inside never take a click. This folds in MAP.121's blocker fade and MAP.141's faint-context rule (contextOpacity, prominence, limitingMagnitude in static/nearfield.js, ready for MAP.148, MAP.150 and MAP.155); nothing is stored or fetched differently.

[8.0.912] - 2026-10-10

Headline: Every planet and moon gets a habitability score and equipment-needed rating.

Added

  • planetgen galaxy and planetgen plan draw one "Whole job (stage N of M)" bar on the command line, with the time elapsed and the time left across all their stages, from the stored stage times (PERF.55). A finished run also stores its whole-job layers per second, counting every layer the scatter stages visited, even those that placed nothing.
  • The galaxy shape settings (Generate page, New galaxy and Customize's Galaxy shape tab, and planetgen plan) now take the density on a spiral arm crest, the density between arms and a core density, with limits and the usual values (1.4, 0.6 and 0 for no core) filled in (ADM.49). The core is extra density at the very centre of the galaxy, on top of the bulge. The bulge amplitude is labelled Bulge density. The Galaxy Map's density model reads the new settings too, and an existing galaxy keeps its density.
  • Scattered black holes and neutron stars store their mass (MAP.165, schema v80), the sector build gives the object that same mass, and the Galaxy Map sizes each point by it, so a 20 solar mass black hole is drawn bigger than a 5 solar mass one and a neutron star smaller than either. The point's tooltip shows the mass. Rows scattered before v80 keep sizing by mass class until the scatter is redone.
  • A Poisson helper that draws a count for any mean in constant time: Knuth below tuning.POISSON_REJECTION_MEAN (10), transformed rejection above it, from the project draw wrapper (PERF.60). The object-first scatter uses it.
  • Every rocky planet and moon description now explains its PHI-4 habitability in full (UX.91): the score and the equipment a human needs, then each of the four colour factors (pressure, temperature, chemistry, radiation) with its colour, this world's input values and the input that sets the colour. The wording matches the Habitability levels page, and the colours always agree with the chip on the system list. Wiki pages carry the same paragraphs.
  • A route between systems now shows travel times for each hop and for the whole trip at every warp and fold factor, with a stop at every system between the ends. Each hop is timed from rest to rest at the factor's constant speed. The stay per stop defaults to 0 minutes and can be changed on the NAV page ("Stay at each stop") or with stay= on GET /api/nav; the response adds warp_times and fold_times to each hop and to the route, plus route.stops and route.stay_minutes. (NAV.11)
  • The Systems page lists the uncharted stars (UX.87): every star the brightness scatter placed that has no system yet, brightest first, with its sector address, ring, layer and slot, galaxy and in-sector coordinates and its own data. An admin can generate one such system by itself with its Generate button (the page recommends generating the whole sector); the sector's other contents stay uncharted. New API: GET /api/uncharted-systems and POST /api/uncharted-systems/<id>/generate.
  • A star, planet, moon, belt or comet link now opens its system page at that body: /system/<id>#planet-12 (and #moon-, #belt-, #comet-, #star-) opens the body's row, highlights it, scrolls to it and selects the body on the System Map. /object/<reference> (for example /object/planet:12) redirects any object reference to the right page or row, and the search results link their bodies this way. Only stars (as their system's page) get pages; planets and moons are anchors. (NAV.8)
  • Generate has one "Redo scatters" box in place of "Rebuild the bright stars" (GEN.196). Tick the scatters to redo (the massive stars, the bright stars, the phenomena), set each one's new limit, and they run as one job with every stage listed and the unticked ones shown as skipped. A scatter clears and rewrites only its own rows, and the central black hole or quasar is always rebuilt. planetgen plan --redo-scatters mass luminosity phenomena does the same from the command line.
  • Random neighborhoods have a "Keep away from filled space" option (planetgen galaxy --avoid-filled-space, random-start mode, and a checkbox on the Generate page). A start whose neighborhood touches a sector that is already generated is dropped, so each neighborhood grows in empty space, and the run says how many candidate centres qualified. (GEN.186)
  • A sector that nothing was generated in opens if a scatter placed something there, marked uncharted (MAP.162). On the Galaxy Map, clicking a sector that is not generated yet, or opening its address (?sector=<designation>&open=1), now flies to it and shows the stars, black holes, neutron stars, quasars, nebulae, remnants and hypervelocity stars the scatters left in it, each in the colour the map gives its kind and each saying in its info panel that its sector is uncharted. The sector carries the mark in three places: its crumb in the title reads "(uncharted)", its info panel is headed "Uncharted sector" with the count of stars and other objects waiting, and a dashed "Uncharted sector ..." tag sits in the corner of the map. Generating the sector replaces all of it with the normal sector view. An empty ungenerated sector is selected as before.
  • GET /api/galaxy/uncharted?ring=&layer=&slot=. One cell's place (designation, centre, edge) and what the scatters left in it (the waiting bright stars and the unbuilt scattered phenomena), with sector_id when the cell has been generated; the web server's /galaxy/uncharted/<ring>/<layer>/<slot>/scene turns it into the map's scene.
  • planetgen check-db --deep now also loads and validates every star system. It prints how long it expects to take (from the speed this server recorded, or a rough guess it says so about), asks for a yes unless --yes is given, shows a progress bar, and lists each failing system. --estimate-only prints just the estimate. The Generate page's "Check the database" section has a "Deep check" option that shows the time and asks you to confirm. (DB.21)
  • Neutron stars and black holes get their own mass limit (GEN.195): --compact-min-mass (1, 2, 4 or 6 solar masses, or star to use the stellar mass limit, the default) and a control beside the stellar mass limit in Plan and New galaxy, with the database cost shown. The central black hole or quasar is always created.
  • A molecular cloud of the galaxy's cloud field (GEN.176) is born in the sector holding the centre of the space it fills, with a field-drawn serial worked out from the galaxy seed alone, so its object ID no longer depends on which sector is saved first. Run-time births (GEN.172) have tests for every path that exists today: a system added to a sector, a phenomenon or system saved on its own, a facility, and a body added by an edit; a number is never given again after its object is deleted.
  • A "Habitability levels" page under Classes (/classes/habitability, UX.90) explains the five equipment levels, the four PHI-4 domains with their Blue, Green, Yellow and Red thresholds, the pulsar, neutron star and black hole host rule, and the Habitable, Habitable moon and Inhabited chips. It is linked from the Classes list, from a visible line above a system's body list and from the Equipment tags on the search page.
  • Object IDs in the database (DB.20, GEN.171): uid is now the 80-bit birth-location ID (BINARY(10), unique on its own) on every object table, and facilities gains the column. The sector fill gives a sector's systems and phenomena their generated serials and a system's bodies their body numbers as the rows are inserted; rows saved later take run-time serials and body numbers from the new id_counters table, whose numbers are never given twice. The schema is v78; existing rows are numbered by row order. The hashed IDs, the bright-sweep systems' position-ID uid and the per-system uniqueness are gone.
  • API keys have scopes (API.9): read, generate, upload and admin (admin implies all; generate and upload imply read), an optional expiry, and a visible prefix. Existing keys become admin keys. A key short of a route's scope gets 403 with required_scope; every key has its own rate limit bucket and skips the per-address defaults; last_used_at is written at most once a minute. The admin page's new-key form takes scopes and a lifetime. Control schema v13.
  • The habitability score of every planet and moon (GEN.89). Each rocky body now stores the PHI-4 display (Pressure, Temperature, Chemistry and Radiation, each a 0 to 1 score and a Blue, Green, Yellow or Red tier, and their overall mean), the microbial-life, complex-life and human-operability numbers behind them, and the equipment a human needs: shirtsleeve, mask, mask and scrubber, sealed suit or full life support. A pulsar's or neutron star's planet always needs full life support. The system page shows the equipment as a coloured chip on every planet and moon row (the tooltip gives the score and what limits it), and the search page has Equipment a Human Needs filters for planets and moons, with the equipment in their result tables. A cosmic-ray change from a nebula or remnant re-scores the body. Schema v76; no new random draws, so seeded output keeps its earlier values and gains these.
  • The object ID layout (GEN.170): galaxy/object_uid.py packs, unpacks, prints and parses the 80-bit ID of birth sector, serial and body number (20 hex digits, BINARY(10)), and picks a longer layout (96 or 128 bits) for a galaxy whose bounds do not fit. Nothing uses it yet; the schema (DB.20) and the fill (GEN.171) come next.
  • The Generate page shows the galaxy's layer specs (ADM.28): how many layers, how tall each is, how far the widest reaches, how many sectors are charted, and a row per layer (an even sample past 41). GET /api/galaxy/shape gives the same as layers.
  • Surface radiation dose, UV and galactic hazards (GEN.87). Every rocky planet and moon now stores its yearly surface dose in mSv (cosmic rays through the air and any dipole, stellar particles, crust and radon, and a cosmic-ray boost while a nebula or remnant presses on its star), a DNA-weighted UV index after the ozone layer, and an ozone-loss flag. Each star stores how many lethal supernovae per Gyr its place in the galaxy brings. Schema v75. Seeded output differs from earlier versions (the crust draws one more value per rocky body).
  • The mass limit (GEN.183) is now picked from the presets 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20 solar masses, 20 by default: a slider in the Generate page's new galaxy and plan forms, and --phenomenon-min-mass on the command line, which refuses any other value. Every star, neutron star and black hole at or above it is placed across the whole galaxy; lighter ones are drawn when their sector is made.
  • Every rocky planet and moon now has a hydrosphere (GEN.88): its water share of its mass, where the water is (dry, in the air, frozen, under ice, open ocean, or a hycean ocean under hydrogen), how much of the surface is ocean and land, the ocean's depth, any ice lid and high-pressure ice beneath, and the ocean's chemistry class (ice-sealed, chloride brine, acid sulfate, soda or neutral) with its pH, water activity and phosphorus supply. Schema v74.

A sector filled later builds its own stars only below the mass and luminosity already placed, a staged scatter tops backfilled sectors up with the lighter stars they lack, and white dwarfs born at 1 solar mass or more are placed too (stored with a NULL lifespan). Schema v79 (sector_stats.bright_mass_sol). Design: docs/design/mass-backfill.md.

Removed

  • Windows support (OPS.39). install.ps1, update.ps1, scripts/deploy-common.ps1, examples/maintenance/install-maintenance-task.ps1, examples/windows/ and docs/deployment/windows.md are gone, as are the Windows CI jobs (windows-jobs, windows-installers), the Windows branches in the code (the detached-process, taskkill and OpenProcess handling of Generate page jobs and the no-Redis fallback to run a job directly, the CPU-percent load reading on the admin queue page, SpawnWorker, the below-normal worker priority class, the checkout-relative log and settings folders, drive-letter disk measuring) and the Windows-only tests. The admin Generate page's jobs now always run on Redis, and the queue page shows only the load average. waitress leaves the server extra and requirements-server.lock.
  • docs/WINDOWS.md gives basic instructions for a typical Windows setup (WSL2 and the Linux guides); anyone who wants native Windows does that work themselves.

Fixed

  • Bookmarks work with object IDs again (TEST.122): the NAV page's "use a bookmark as start or destination" list and the sector picker had stopped listing any bookmark since systems, sectors and phenomena were named by their printed ID instead of a row number.
  • The test that a loaded sector knows every object's cell and velocity no longer fails about one run in 300: it drew a system whose only planet had no place in the galaxy, and now draws again until one has (TEST.123).
  • The Galaxy Map's "Dimmest star shown" slider says "every star" only when the view holds every star there is (an open sector). At galaxy scale, where tiles are capped and some sectors are uncharted, it names the dimmest star the view actually carries (MAP.166).
  • Galaxy Map: the "Dimmest star shown" slider now runs from the dimmest to the brightest star the current view's tiles actually carry, at galaxy scale too, instead of stopping at a fixed 2,500 solar luminosities (MAP.163 follow-up). 0 still shows every star.
  • Galaxy Map: the galactic nucleus now shows from the whole-galaxy view whether it is a quasar or a supermassive black hole, and stays there once its sector is filled (MAP.164 follow-up). The nucleus quasar was missing from the scattered objects the map lists.
  • ./update.sh step 8 ("Checking the cache, jobs and debug log locations") no longer fails with FileNotFoundError on util/appconfig.py; setup-debug-log.sh now loads the log paths from util/logpaths.py, so the logs and their rotation are set up again. Two new tests (the log-location check runs against the checkout; deploy scripts only name repo paths that exist) fail on the old script.
  • The star scatter pass tests use a luminosity floor the toy galaxy can fill with lighter stars, since the real floor now starts at 2,500 solar luminosities (GEN.184).

[8.0.866] - 2026-10-10

Headline: Star scatter runs in mass and luminosity passes with preset limits.

Changed

  • GEN.175: regenerating a phenomenon keeps its uid; it was set to NULL.
  • Docs only: filed GEN.187 (bright-star back scatter by mass, issue #952), MAP.162 (open sectors that hold scattered objects but were never generated, issue #928) and UX.87 (uncharted systems in the system list, issue #929).
  • Docs only: filed TEST.115 (Windows CI leg failures: Redis in WSL unreachable) and TEST.116 (a one-off K2V failure in test_bughunt_end_to_end) from the Bugfixes lane 1 CI findings.
  • GitHub CI (ci.yml, every test leg) now runs only by hand: Actions > CI > Run workflow. It no longer runs on a push or a pull request. stamp-version.yml and release-note.yml are unchanged.
  • CI: the linux-update job's "needs migrating" and "failed migration" steps rebuild the database from the v61 baseline fixture (the oldest schema update.sh upgrades from) instead of faking v48, which the code has refused since the Alembic cleanup. The old steps failed with "database is at schema v48, older than v61".
  • Docs only: TEST.112 (the 8 s wait for queued API edits, PR #955) is retired from the TODO list and the plans; TEST.111 stays open with a note.
  • TEST.112: tests now wait up to 120 s for a queued API edit instead of 8 s, so a slow worker start in a busy parallel run no longer turns a 200 into a 202 (the cause of the intermittent test_regenerate_phenomenon_keeps_id_name_and_place failure). TEST.111's assertions now print the results they checked, so its next failure names the cause.
  • Docs only: GEN.185 (the five-pass scatter, PR #953, schema v73) is retired from the TODO list and the plans; the next free Alembic revision is 0074.
  • The star scatter runs in passes (GEN.185). The mass pass places every star born at or above the mass limit (the same 8 to 20 solar mass limit as the phenomenon scatter's, default 20), whatever its luminosity. Each sector holding one at least as bright as the luminosity floor is marked, and the luminosity pass then places the lighter stars at least that bright and skips the marked sectors, which already hold a star that bright. A sector's own draw is lighter than the limit and dimmer than the floor, and the backfill and the staged bands below the floor draw only lighter stars too. This changes the stars a given seed gives: re-plan the galaxy (planetgen plan) to get the new scatter.
  • galaxy_shape.bright_star_mass_limit_sol (schema v73) records the mass limit the star scatter used; a galaxy scattered before it keeps NULL and behaves as before.
  • Docs only: GEN.97 (random neighborhoods, PR #950) is retired from the TODO list and the plans; GEN.186 files the leftover "keep away from filled space" option.
  • Docs only: GEN.165 (a test bug about a comet round a second star, PR #948) is retired from the TODO list and the plans.
  • GEN.165: the epoch-position test compared a comet round a second star with the barycenter; it now compares against what the comet goes round, like planets, so it no longer fails in some random systems. No product code was wrong.
  • Docs only: TEST.114 (exact COUNT(*) in the check test, PR #946) is retired from the TODO list and the plans.
  • TEST.114: the "check writes nothing" test compares exact row counts instead of MySQL's background-refreshed row estimates, so it no longer fails under load.
  • The System Map no longer shows a comet on an open (parabolic) orbit once its pass is over (or before it arrives): beyond the drawn path, 2,000 AU out, it disappears instead of flying on forever. Closed-orbit comets always show.
  • Docs only: recorded Boss's answers on NAV.8 (stars only get pages), NAV.11 (stay per stop defaults to 0 minutes, user-changeable) and API.23 (the object ID replaces row ids, API break accepted).

  • Every generation and maintenance step reports its progress through one helper (planetgen.generation.steps): a bar is drawn by itself at the start of a step predicted to take longer than 15 seconds from the speeds this server recorded for its kind, nothing is drawn for a shorter one, and a step that runs past 15 seconds gets its bar at that moment. A step with no recorded speed yet is treated as long, so a first run still shows its bar. Finished steps record their speed back, so the next prediction has history; the Stats page lists each kind.
  • The sector bars, neighbour linking, sector paths, bright-star backfill and top-up, the phenomenon scatter (now timed in the bar's own units, so its bar starts from a recorded rate too), the population pass, reset and the orbit update draw through it. Steps inside a worker can report to the parent through a channel (worker_step and Relay).

  • A rocky planet that no tide has slowed now turns in 8 to 48 hours, drawn log-uniform as giant-impact formation models give (Kokubo and Genda 2010), instead of anywhere from 10 to 1,400 hours. Slow days now come only from tidal locking. Most unlocked rocky planets with a working dynamo now get a dipole field instead of a multipolar one (GEN.86 follow-up, Boss's decision of 2026-10-10).   • Parallel generation workers no longer queue for the system-name registry: each save claims its names in a short transaction of its own instead of holding the registry's row locks until the whole sector commits. In a dense core, 8 sectors on 4 workers took 54 s instead of about 90 s. A claim is given back if the save fails, and a first holder that a later save wanted to rename renames itself when it commits (PERF.49). Names, bodies and registry rows are the same as before on a seeded run.
  • Name reservation looks a name's candidates up by key instead of scanning the whole sector for each name, and the offensive-word check is one compiled pattern (PERF.49).

  • The phenomenon scatter places only the neutron stars and black holes of at least 20 solar masses (GEN.166 to GEN.168), so planetgen plan writes about 2.7e5 phenomenon rows instead of about 1.17e9. A sector draws the lighter ones itself when it is filled, from its own stream, so the galaxy holds the same number of each. --phenomenon-min-mass sets the cut and --phenomena-only re-scatters at a new one; the cut is stored with the scatter (schema v71) and in the settings file. Stellar-mass and intermediate-mass black holes are now drawn as separate kinds. This is the second half of the one-time reseed that began with lazy names (PERF.43): the same seed now gives a different galaxy than before both changes.
  • Retired PERF.44, PERF.45 and ADM.48 (PR #863); PERF.46 keeps only its finite_domain question.
  • A saved sector's rows now get their unique ID in the INSERT instead of being selected back and updated afterwards, which saves a query pass per sector (PERF.44). The IDs are the same.
  • A galaxy run now links its new sectors to their neighbours (containment in nebulae and remnants, nearest systems) once at its end instead of one sector at a time while it saves, so the workers no longer queue for it (PERF.45). The stored links are the same. Sectors made on demand still link as they are saved.
  • A planet's or moon's position is worked out once when first read instead of after every move (PERF.46); the values are unchanged.
  • Retired PERF.43 (PR #861) and filed ADM.48, the failing auth-sweep tests for the galaxy-settings download.
  • Stars and phenomena draw their generated name only when it is first read (PERF.43). A placed phenomenon is named by its object ID and never draws one, which saves about 4 percent of a sector fill; building a rogue planet is about four times faster. This is the first half of a one-time reseed: each name now takes one draw at construction instead of many, so the same seed gives a different galaxy. The second half is the 20 solar mass phenomenon cut (GEN.166 to GEN.168).

The seed stays an internal mechanism for parallel workers, fills, backfills and settle.
